items.subject: surgery
items.title: Scalpel
items.caption: Remember: Bard-Parker handle No.
items.author: SnowBink

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Superficial spreading melanoma
items.caption: Remember: superficial spreading melanoma is the commonest melanoma subtype, with a radial growth phase showing pagetoid spread and junctional nests of atypical melanocytes.
items.author: Juliana Casagrande Tavoloni Braga, Mariana Petaccia Macedo, Clovis Pinto, João Duprat, Maria Dirlei

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve
items.caption: Remember: the left RLN hooks around the ligamentum arteriosum (aortic arch), the right RLN around the right subclavian artery; the left is at risk in station 4L/5 node dissection.
items.author: Hideyuki Wada, Yasuhiro Hida, Kichizo Kaga, Ryunosuke Hase, Kazuto Ohtaka, Jun Muto, Nakada-Kubota R

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Complete right bronchial rupture with disruption of the bronchus intermedius
items.caption: Remember: Blunt chest trauma + persistent air leak despite chest tube + 'fallen lung' sign = tracheobronchial rupture; most occur within 2.5 cm of the carina, right more often than left, confirmed by bronchoscopy.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Triquetral bone
items.caption: Remember: Triquetral = pyramidal, ulnar-most of the proximal row, carries the pisiform anteriorly and articulates with the hamate; the second most commonly fractured carpal bone (dorsal avulsion chip fracture).
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Iliopsoas and pectineus
items.caption: Floor of femoral triangle = Iliopsoas (lateral) + Pectineus (medial); borders: inguinal ligament (base), sartorius (lateral), adductor longus (medial); contents NAVEL from lateral to medial.
items.author: Daniel G. Bates

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red stains amyloid orange-red, with apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: Surgeon's knot = double wrap in the first throw (2-1-1), giving friction that prevents slippage when tissue is under tension.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgical metallic clips following cholecystectomy
items.caption: Remember: metallic clips after cholecystectomy appear as bright, linear, metal-density foci with streak artifact in the gallbladder fossa; they are an expected finding, not a retained stone.
items.author: Hellerhoff

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Buruli ulcer
items.caption: Remember: Buruli ulcer = M.
items.author: Humberto Guerra, Juan Carlos Palomino, Eduardo Falconí, Francisco Bravo, Ninoska Donaires, Eric Van

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Nodular melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Nodular melanoma lacks a radial growth phase, grows vertically, presents as a rapidly enlarging, often amelanotic or bleeding nodule, and is usually thick at diagnosis.
items.author: Image courtesy of Dr. Ahmet Cemil Kaur Article authors: Zekayi Kutlubay, Burhan Engin, Server Serdar

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Melanoma of the grey horse
items.caption: Remember: grey horse melanoma shows sheets of heavily melanin-laden cells (STX17 duplication linked to greying), occurs at the perianal region and tail base, and is slow growing with low metastatic tendency.
items.author: Alex brollo

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Superficial dissection of the upper arm and axilla (medial view) showing brachial artery, basilic and cephalic veins, median and ulnar nerves
items.caption: Remember: the brachial artery lies medial to the biceps, with the median nerve crossing anterior to it from lateral to medial at mid-arm, and the basilic vein piercing the deep fascia to join the brachial veins.
items.author: George Henry Ford

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mayo-Hegar needle holder
items.caption: Remember: A needle holder has short, stout jaws with crosshatching, ring handles, and a ratchet lock.
items.author: Olek Remesz (wiki-pl: Orem , commons: Orem )

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Left tubal ectopic pregnancy with hematosalpinx
items.caption: Remember: a focal bluish, bulging ampullary tube with blood in the pouch of Douglas on laparoscopy means tubal ectopic pregnancy (ampulla is the commonest site, isthmus the commonest site to rupture early).
items.author: Urskalberer81

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Human pancreas
items.caption: Remember: Pancreas = densely packed basophilic serous acini + pale islets of Langerhans + centroacinar cells, with NO striated ducts (unlike salivary glands).
items.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Keloid
items.caption: Remember: keloid = thick, glassy, hypereosinophilic haphazard collagen bundles that extend beyond the original wound; hypertrophic scar stays within the wound margin and has parallel nodular collagen with myofibroblasts.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gluteus medius
items.caption: Remember: Gluteus medius arises between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines, inserts on the lateral surface of the greater trochanter, is supplied by the superior gluteal nerve, and its weakness causes a positive Trendelenburg sign.
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile (wild-type transthyretin) cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Senile cardiac amyloidosis = wild-type transthyretin (ATTR) in elderly men, restrictive cardiomyopathy, no monoclonal protein, Congo red apple-green birefringence, better prognosis than AL.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Scapula with humerus, radius, ulna and bones of the hand (upper limb skeleton)
items.caption: Remember: the upper limb skeleton runs scapula (glenoid) - humerus - radius and ulna - 8 carpals - 5 metacarpals - 14 phalanges.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Smellie's obstetrical forceps
items.caption: Remember: Smellie introduced the English lock, the pelvic curve, and leather-covered blades.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
items.caption: Remember: Canal of Nuck = female counterpart of the processus vaginalis.
items.author: Nakamura, K., Higashiguchi, T., Chikaishi, Y. et al.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Farabeuf bone-holding forceps
items.caption: Remember: Farabeuf (davier) = bone-holding forceps with serrated, offset jaws and long slender handles, used to grip and reduce fracture fragments.
items.author: Joséphine Bitat

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Bladder retractor
items.caption: Remember: the bladder retractor is a one-sided, hand-held retractor with a wide concave blade and a ring-and-hook handle, used to depress the bladder in hysterectomy, caesarean section, and urological surgery.
items.author: SnowBink

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Incus strut (interposition) prosthesis between malleus and stapes capitulum
items.caption: Remember: Incus interposition strut = malleus handle to stapes capitulum (intact superstructure).
items.author: Jack M. Kartush, MD

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: the atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process; it is a ring with two lateral masses and bears the skull.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Paratubal cysts
items.caption: Remember: paratubal (paraovarian) cysts are extra-ovarian, thin-walled, often pedunculated cysts in the broad ligament/mesosalpinx from Wolffian or Mullerian remnants (e.g., hydatid of Morgagni); they predispose to adnexal torsion.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Burkitt lymphoma
items.caption: Remember: Burkitt lymphoma = starry-sky histology + basophilic cytoplasm with lipid vacuoles on Wright-Giemsa + t(8;14) MYC + Ki-67 about 100%; endemic form presents as a jaw mass with EBV.
items.author: Ed Uthman, MD.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis induced by infective endocarditis
items.caption: Remember: crescents plus granular C3 on IF in a febrile patient with a murmur and positive blood cultures means infective endocarditis-associated GN (often S.
items.author: Daisuke Koya, Kazuyuki Shibuya, Ryuichi Kikkawa and Masakazu Haneda.

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: Atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process, carries the skull on its concave superior facets, and a burst fracture of its ring is a Jefferson fracture.
items.author: Jlabanimation

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Recurrent inguinal hernia due to defect of the fascia transversalis after Bassini repair
items.caption: Remember: the Bassini repair is a tension-based tissue repair (conjoint tendon to inguinal ligament) with a higher recurrence rate; recurrent hernia after an anterior repair is best treated by a posterior (laparoscopic) mesh approach.
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pectoral (shoulder) girdle viewed from above
items.caption: Remember: the pectoral girdle (clavicle + scapula) is incomplete posteriorly and attaches to the axial skeleton only via the sternoclavicular joint, whereas the pelvic girdle is a complete, stable ring.
items.author: Bobjgalindo

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Femoral triangle
items.caption: Femoral triangle: base is the inguinal ligament, lateral border sartorius, medial border adductor longus.
items.author: Daniel G. Bates

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Lentigo maligna melanoma = elderly, chronic sun-damaged face, confluent atypical melanocytes with adnexal (follicular) extension and solar elastosis; Melan A/SOX10 confirm melanocytic origin.
items.author: Robert M. Hurwitz, Larry J. Buckel, Don-John Summerlin

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Bistoury knife
items.caption: Remember: Scalpel handle No.
items.author: SnowBink

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Complete disruption of the right intermediate bronchus just below the origin of the right upper lobe bronchus
items.caption: Blunt chest trauma + persistent air leak after chest tube + non-expanding lung (+/- 'fallen lung' sign) = tracheobronchial rupture, usually within 2 cm of the carina, right side more common; confirm with bronchoscopy and CT 3D airway reconstruction.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Brain-infiltrating metastatic melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Melanoma is the great mimicker; discohesive epithelioid cells with eccentric nuclei, macronucleoli, hemorrhage and brown pigment in a brain lesion = melanoma (S100, SOX10, HMB-45, Melan-A positive).
items.author: Jensflorian

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red gives apple-green birefringence under polarized light, which is the hallmark of amyloid in any organ.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: mrcp-cardiology
items.title: Rheumatic heart disease
items.caption: Aschoff bodies and Anitschkow cells are the histological hallmarks of acute rheumatic carditis, and mitral stenosis is the most common valve lesion in chronic disease.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Fasciotomy
items.caption: Remember: Acute compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis (pain on passive stretch); treat with urgent fasciotomy, leaving the wound open for delayed closure or skin grafting.
items.author: Sarte at English Wikipedia ( Original text: Sarte )

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Malignant melanoma in situ
items.caption: Remember: Melanoma in situ = atypical melanocytes confined to the epidermis with pagetoid upward spread and nests of varying size, without dermal invasion.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Axis-traction obstetric forceps (Corning type)
items.caption: Remember: A detachable curved rod with a cross-bar handle attached to the blades means axis-traction forceps (Tarnier, Milne-Murray, Corning).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Percy retractor
items.caption: Remember: the Percy retractor is a split metal disc with a central hole that holds the soft-tissue cuff proximally during amputation, so the bone is cut higher than the soft tissue and the stump is well covered.
items.author: Joséphine Bitat

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Classical chordoma
items.caption: Remember: Chordoma = midline sacrum/clivus tumor with physaliferous (bubbly vacuolated) cells in myxoid matrix; cytokeratin+, EMA+, S-100+, brachyury+ (most specific).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Membranous nephropathy = adult nephrotic syndrome, thick capillary walls without hypercellularity, silver stain spikes, subepithelial deposits on EM, anti-PLA2R positive, granular IgG on IF.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Aditus of larynx
items.caption: Remember: the aditus of larynx = epiglottis (anterior), aryepiglottic folds (lateral), interarytenoid fold (posterior); it is oblique and faces posterosuperiorly.
items.author: Anatomist90

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Adult nephrotic syndrome + diffusely thickened capillary walls without hypercellularity = membranous nephropathy (spikes on silver stain, subepithelial deposits on EM, anti-PLA2R positive).
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Small intestine (jejunoileum) with its mesentery
items.caption: Remember: small bowel = plicae circulares, arcades with vasa recta, no taeniae, haustra or appendices epiploicae.
items.author: Anatomist90

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: The axis (C2) is the only cervical vertebra with a dens (odontoid process); hangman's fracture is a bilateral C2 pars interarticularis fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma
items.caption: Remember: Gallbladder carcinoma is usually an adenocarcinoma arising in a gallstone-associated, chronically inflamed gallbladder and is often found incidentally.
items.author: Unknown / Public domain

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Slotted Foerster forceps
items.caption: Remember: Foerster (sponge-holding) forceps = long, ratcheted, ring-shaped fenestrated jaws used for swabs, skin prep and gentle tissue holding.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. Pascal666 assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Wilms' tumor = triphasic (blastema + epithelial tubules/abortive glomeruli + stroma); a child aged 2-5 years with a flank mass that does not cross the midline, plus hypertension; WT1 (11p13) and WT2 (11p15).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Internal iliac artery
items.caption: Remember: The internal iliac artery divides into an anterior and a posterior division.
items.author: Dr. Johannes Sobotta

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Scalpel (bistoury) with detachable blade
items.caption: Remember: Blade No. 21 (large curved belly) fits the No.
items.author: SnowBink

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Omental bursa (lesser sac)
items.caption: Remember: the lesser sac lies behind the stomach and lesser omentum and communicates with the greater sac only via the epiploic foramen of Winslow (bounded anteriorly by the free edge of the lesser omentum with portal triad).
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile (wild-type transthyretin) cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: an elderly man with HFpEF, thick ventricles, low-voltage ECG and no M-protein has wild-type ATTR (senile) amyloid.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheotomy set
items.caption: Remember: A tracheotomy set = scalpel + tracheal hook + tracheal dilator + curved flanged tracheostomy tubes (with brush for cleaning); classic historical indication was diphtheria.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hagedorn needle holder
items.caption: Remember: Hagedorn needle holder is a ratchet-locked needle driver for flat, curved, cutting Hagedorn needles used in skin closure; Mayo-Hegar is the heavy general-purpose driver, Castroviejo the delicate microsurgical one.
items.author: Grey Geezer

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic malignant melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Hemorrhagic brain metastases - melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, thyroid carcinoma.
items.author: Jensflorian

items.subject: mrcp-cardiology
items.title: Necrotic lipid-rich core with overlying fibrous cap and intraplaque haemorrhage
items.caption: Symptomatic carotid stenosis of 50 to 99% warrants carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of the event under NICE NG128, provided surgical risk is acceptable.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheotomy set
items.caption: Remember: A tracheotomy set = graded curved cannulae (outer and inner tube) with neck flanges, tracheal dilator, tenaculum hook, scissors and forceps; emergency airway in diphtheria is a classic indication.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Bony orbit containing the globe with the rectus muscle insertions
items.caption: Remember: the four recti arise from the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) and insert on the sclera anterior to the equator.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. Patrick.lynch assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Pheochromocytoma
items.caption: Remember: pheochromocytoma = zellballen nests of granular basophilic cells with S100+ sustentacular cells, chromogranin+, and bizarre nuclei that do not indicate malignancy.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Parosteal osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Parosteal osteosarcoma = posterior distal femur surface lesion, 'stuck-on' ossified mass, parallel bony trabeculae with bland spindle stroma, MDM2/CDK4 amplification; good prognosis unless dedifferentiated.
items.author: 藤澤孝志

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Triple pelvic osteotomy for acetabular reorientation
items.caption: Remember: Salter = 1 cut (ilium), Triple = 3 cuts (ilium, pubis, ischium) when symphysis is stiff; Pemberton = incomplete cut hinging on open triradiate cartilage; Chiari = salvage with medial displacement; Ganz PAO = adults, posterior column intact.
items.author: siehe Quelle, Veränderungen von mir selbst

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
items.caption: Remember: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy = 4 ports (umbilical camera, epigastric, 2 right subcostal 5 mm) and the gallbladder is usually extracted via the umbilical port; always obtain the critical view of safety.
items.author: Nankai

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Cross-section of the lower thoracic spinal cord
items.caption: Remember: the lateral horn (T1-L2) and Clarke dorsal nucleus (C8-L3) with a slender H-shaped gray matter and abundant white matter identify a thoracic cord section.
items.author: Dr. Johannes Sobotta

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Flexor carpi radialis
items.caption: Remember: FCR runs from the medial epicondyle to the palmar bases of metacarpals II (and III); the radial pulse is felt just lateral to its tendon, and it is the only wrist flexor with a median nerve supply other than palmaris longus (and flexor digitorum superficialis for fingers).
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Iliacus
items.caption: Remember: Iliacus = iliac fossa to lesser trochanter (with psoas major as iliopsoas); femoral nerve (L2-L3); chief hip flexor.
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgical hook, 3-toothed sharp
items.caption: Remember: A 3-toothed sharp hook (rake retractor) retracts skin and superficial tissue; the blunt variant is used to protect delicate tissue.
items.author: Vdovinweb

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Split-thickness meshed skin graft showing early take, supported by negative pressure wound therapy
items.caption: Remember: a meshed split-thickness skin graft shows a diamond lattice pattern; a pink adherent graft at day 5 means take, and VAC over a graft prevents seroma, hematoma, and shear.
items.author: Paul Farrant Original uploader was El gordo 78 at en.wikipedia

items.subject: pathology
items.title: High-grade osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Malignant cells producing osteoid (pink, glassy, homogeneous matrix) = osteosarcoma, regardless of how much cartilage or spindle-cell area is present.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: the axis (C2) is the only cervical vertebra with a dens (odontoid process).
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheotomy set
items.caption: Remember: a curved, flanged metal tube plus a sharp tracheal hook, a blunt dilator and a scalpel equals a tracheotomy set.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior inferior iliac spine
items.caption: Remember: AIIS = straight head of rectus femoris + iliofemoral ligament; ASIS = sartorius + inguinal ligament.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Torus tubarius
items.caption: Remember: the torus tubarius is formed by the tubal cartilage; the fossa of Rosenmuller lies behind it (the commonest site of nasopharyngeal carcinoma), while the levator veli palatini forms the torus levatorius below the ostium.
items.author: S. SIMKINS, PH.D.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Needle holder
items.caption: Remember: a needle holder has short, stout jaws with fine cross-hatched or transverse serrations (often a central groove or carbide insert) to hold the needle at the junction of its distal one-third and proximal two-thirds, whereas artery forceps have long, tapered jaws.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Amyloid = Congo red positive (pink-red) with apple-green birefringence under polarized light; vascular deposition causes GI bleeding and fragility.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Lentigo maligna melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Lentigo maligna = melanoma in situ on chronically sun-damaged head/neck of the elderly; once it invades the dermis it becomes lentigo maligna melanoma.
items.author: Omar Bari, Philip R. Cohen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Radius and ulna
items.caption: Remember: the ulna is the stable, medial forearm bone with the olecranon proximally.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Femoral triangle
items.caption: Remember: Femoral triangle = inguinal ligament (base), sartorius (lateral), adductor longus (medial); floor = iliopsoas + pectineus (+ adductor longus); contents lateral to medial = NAVEL (Nerve, Artery, Vein, Empty space, Lymphatics).
items.author: Double-M from Athens, GA, USA

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Left tubal ectopic pregnancy with hematosalpinx
items.caption: Remember: the ampulla is the most common site of tubal ectopic pregnancy.
items.author: Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Écorché wax anatomical model showing superficial muscles and bones
items.caption: Remember: Écorché means 'flayed', a figure with skin removed to show superficial muscles.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acute subchorionic intervillositis (placentitis)
items.caption: Remember: neutrophils in the subchorionic fibrinoid/intervillous space = acute subchorionic intervillositis (acute placentitis), usually from ascending infection with preterm labor; lymphocytes/histiocytes = chronic lesions.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Posterior aspect of right forearm and hand, showing deep muscles
items.caption: Remember: the deep extensor layer is supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve, which pierces the supinator.
items.author: George A. Piersol

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Medial epicondyle
items.caption: Remember: the medial epicondyle gives origin to the common flexor tendon and the ulnar nerve passes behind it, so medial epicondyle injury in a child gives ulnar nerve symptoms.
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis
items.caption: Remember: crescents (more than 50 percent of glomeruli) plus hypocomplementemia in SLE means severe proliferative lupus nephritis presenting as RPGN.
items.author: Satoshi Suzuki, Kei Ogiwara, Takuya Nishi, Shota Sakuma, Maiko Akira, Masako Iwasaki, Daisuke Honda,

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Typical cervical vertebra (C3-C6)
items.caption: Remember: foramen transversarium + bifid spinous process + triangular vertebral foramen = typical cervical vertebra (C3-C6); C1 has no body, and C2 has the dens.
items.author: Altick

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Ulcerated, endophytic adenocarcinoma of the colon
items.caption: Remember: left-sided colon cancer is typically annular or ulcerative and causes obstruction and altered bowel habit; right-sided colon cancer is polypoid or exophytic and causes iron deficiency anemia.
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor of the jejunum
items.caption: Remember: GIST = exophytic, hypervascular, extraluminal mass from the bowel wall, often bleeding with normal endoscopy; CD117/DOG1 positive; treat with R0 resection (no lymphadenectomy) +/- imatinib.
items.author: Hellerhoff

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Bronchial stenosis at the site of surgical repair of the right bronchus
items.caption: Remember: after blunt trauma, tracheobronchial rupture occurs within 2 cm of the carina (right more often); a repaired bronchus can later develop anastomotic stenosis, best shown by 3D CT reconstruction or bronchoscopy.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic appendicectomy
items.caption: Remember: In laparoscopic appendicectomy, follow the taenia coli to the caecal base to find the appendix, control the mesoappendix (appendicular artery) first, then ligate the base and divide it.
items.author: Life-of-hannes.de at German Wikipedia

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Benign nasal squamous papilloma
items.caption: Remember: Nasal vestibule papilloma = exophytic, keratinizing squamous, HPV 6/11.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Fuller's bivalve metal tracheostomy tube
items.caption: Remember: Fuller's tube = bivalve (two-bladed) metal tracheostomy tube, helpful for easy insertion in obese or short-necked patients and a deep trachea; Jackson's tube = metal with an inner tube.
items.author: Sarindam7

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lateral ventricle
items.caption: Remember: the lateral ventricle has 3 horns plus a body.
items.author: John A Beal , PhD Dep't. of Cellular Biology & Anatomy, Louisiana State University Health Sciences C

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Right inguinal hernia with an extended sac
items.caption: Remember: inguinal hernias lie ABOVE and medial to the pubic tubercle (femoral hernias lie below and lateral to it); CT showing bowel or fat in a sac along the spermatic cord confirms the diagnosis and detects strangulation.
items.author: Shigeru Fujisaki, Motoi Takashina, Ryouichi Tomita and Ken-Ichi Sakurai

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix
items.caption: Remember: Cervical SCC (HPV 16 most common) is graded by keratinization and differentiation; poorly differentiated tumours show solid sheets of pleomorphic cells with minimal keratin, and diffuse p16 and p63/p40 positivity confirm it.
items.author: Li H, Jing X, Yu J, Liu J, Zhang T, Chen S

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Follicular lymphoma
items.caption: Remember: Follicular lymphoma = t(14;18), BCL2 overexpression, nodular pattern of centrocytes and centroblasts (peripheral nucleoli), CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2+, indolent course.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
items.caption: Remember: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck is the female equivalent of an encysted hydrocele of the cord, due to a patent processus vaginalis along the round ligament; treat with excision and high ligation of the sac.
items.author: Nakamura, K., Higashiguchi, T., Chikaishi, Y. et al.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Neurocysticercosis (intraventricular cysticercus cyst)
items.caption: Remember: Intraventricular (fourth ventricle) cysticercus causes obstructive hydrocephalus.
items.author: Michael J. Kavanaugh

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: The sphenoid is the unpaired, butterfly-shaped keystone of the cranial base.
items.author: Wmpearl

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Wolf forceps (Vrikamukha swastikayantra)
items.caption: Remember: Sushruta's swastikayantra are 24 cross-shaped hinged forceps named after animal and bird faces (simha, vrika, krauncha, etc.), used mainly to extract foreign bodies.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Thyroid resection (goiter surgery) through a collar incision with a retractor system
items.caption: Remember: Goiter surgery = collar (Kocher) incision, strap muscle retraction, identify the recurrent laryngeal nerve and preserve the parathyroids; frame retractors give hands-free exposure through small incisions.
items.author: THWZ

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: the pterion is formed by the frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of the sphenoid; it overlies the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery (extradural haematoma).
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pars distalis of the anterior pituitary with chromophobes, basophils, and acidophils
items.caption: Remember: the pars distalis has three cell types on H&E: acidophils (GH, prolactin), basophils (ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH), and chromophobes (degranulated or stem cells).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Ewing sarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Ewing sarcoma is a small round blue cell tumor with PAS-positive, diastase-sensitive glycogen, CD99 positivity and t(11;22) EWSR1-FLI1.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Palmar view of wrist joint dissection
items.caption: Remember: the pronator quadratus on the anterior distal radius and ulna, with the pisiform and hamate hook on the ulnar side of the carpus, identifies a palmar (volar) wrist dissection.
items.author: Anatomist90 , Arabic Derivative: Elbasyouny

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: the atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process; its body is donated to the axis as the dens.
items.author: MAKY.OREL

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Malignant melanoma
items.caption: Remember: HMB-45 (gp100) is the specific melanoma marker, S-100 and SOX10 are the most sensitive, and Melan-A (MART-1) is the other commonly used marker.
items.author: Jensflorian

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Split-thickness skin graft donor site
items.caption: Remember: a split-thickness graft donor site is a clean, uniform partial-thickness wound with punctate bleeding points.
items.author: Ericalens

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Thoracic duct
items.caption: Remember: the thoracic duct lies between the azygos vein and the descending aorta (the 'duct between two vessels') behind the oesophagus, crosses from right to left at T5, and drains into the left jugulo-subclavian junction.
items.author: René van der Bel

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lungs of a human embryo at a more advanced stage of development, with lobar (secondary) bronchial buds (three on the right, two on the left)
items.caption: Remember: lobar (secondary) bronchi appear at 5 to 6 weeks as 3 on the right and 2 on the left; segmental bronchi (10 right, 8 to 9 left) follow at 7 weeks.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Capitate
items.caption: Remember: the capitate is the largest carpal bone, sits in the center of the distal row, and articulates with the base of the 3rd metacarpal.
items.author: Photo is by Brian C. Goss

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: membranous nephropathy = adult nephrotic syndrome, GBM spikes on silver stain, subepithelial deposits on EM, anti-PLA2R antibodies, with a risk of renal vein thrombosis.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: Crescent = parietal epithelial cells + macrophages + fibrin in Bowman space; RPGN is diagnosed with crescents in >50% of glomeruli.
items.author: Unknown / Public domain

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Latissimus dorsi
items.caption: Remember: Latissimus dorsi = thoracolumbar fascia + iliac crest + lower 3-4 ribs + inferior scapular angle, inserts in the floor of the bicipital groove; supplied by the thoracodorsal nerve (C6-C8); the 'climber's muscle' that extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: mrcp-cardiology
items.title: Acute rheumatic carditis
items.caption: Aschoff bodies (fibrinoid necrosis with Anitschkow cells) are pathognomonic of acute rheumatic carditis; the 2015 revised Jones criteria require evidence of preceding group A streptococcal infection.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile (wild-type transthyretin) cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Senile cardiac amyloidosis = wild-type transthyretin in elderly men, restrictive cardiomyopathy with thick walls and low voltage ECG, Congo red positive with apple-green birefringence, no monoclonal protein; treat with tafamidis.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Small cell osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: A small round blue cell tumor of bone with tumor osteoid is small cell osteosarcoma, not Ewing sarcoma.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Nasal retractor (nasal speculum type)
items.caption: Remember: a nasal retractor or speculum has small ball-tipped blades, a spring and a thumb screw.
items.author: Joe Mabel

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: Hydrocoele of the canal of Nuck = female counterpart of encysted hydrocoele of the cord (patent processus vaginalis along the round ligament); treat with excision and high ligation of the sac.
items.author: Livia Bressan

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: A tracheotomy set = graded curved tubes with a neck flange and tapes + introducer + tracheal dilator; the tracheal incision is made at the 2nd-3rd rings, below the thyroid isthmus.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hepatic cystic echinococcosis (hydatid cyst)
items.caption: Remember: in hepatic hydatid disease, avoid spillage of cyst contents, which can cause anaphylaxis and secondary seeding.
items.author: Haitao Li, Yingmei Shao, Tuerganaili Aji, Jinhui Zhang, Kafayat Kashif, Qinglong Ma, Bo Ran and Hao

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tongue-holding forceps
items.caption: Remember: tongue-holding forceps have broad fenestrated oval serrated jaws with a ratchet.
items.author: Citizen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acute appendicitis
items.caption: Remember: Acute appendicitis is diagnosed histologically by neutrophils in the muscularis propria; grossly, the appendix is swollen and congested with a dull fibrinopurulent serosal exudate.
items.author: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical college

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Caecum after laparoscopic removal of the vermiform appendix
items.caption: Remember: the three taeniae coli of the caecum converge at the base of the appendix, guiding the surgeon to it during laparoscopic appendicectomy; McBurney's point lies at the junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the line from the ASIS to the umbilicus.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Fibularis longus tendon
items.caption: Remember: fibularis longus passes behind the lateral malleolus (superficial to brevis), grooves the cuboid, crosses the sole, and inserts on the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal base; it everts the foot and is supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.
items.author: Whoisjohngalt

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: the sphenoid is the 'keystone' of the cranial base.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Left elbow joint (humerus, radius and ulna)
items.caption: Remember: the elbow is a composite synovial joint with three articulations (humeroulnar, humeroradial, proximal radioulnar) enclosed in a single capsule.
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Red: left anterior descending artery; Yellow: left circumflex artery
items.caption: Remember: LAD supplies the anterior LV wall, apex and anterior 2/3 of the septum (V1-V4).
items.author: Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Trephine
items.caption: Remember: a trephine has a hollow, serrated circular crown on a shaft and cuts a disc of bone.
items.author: Scanned by User:Rmrfstar from page 33 of: Singer, Charles & Underwood, E. Ashworth (1962), Short His

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Ethmoid bone
items.caption: Remember: the ethmoid bone has the crista galli, cribriform plate, perpendicular plate, superior and middle conchae, uncinate process and bulla ethmoidalis.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
items.caption: Remember: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck is the female equivalent of a spermatic cord hydrocele.
items.author: Fikatas, P.; Megas, I.-F.; Mantouvalou, K.; Alkatout, I.; Chopra, S.S.; Biebl, M.; Pratschke, J.; Ra

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Debakey forceps
items.caption: Remember: Debakey = atraumatic vascular forceps with fine longitudinal serrations along the tips and no teeth.
items.author: Phyo WP

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Écorché figure (flayed-body model showing superficial muscles and vessels)
items.caption: Remember: Écorché = 'flayed' figure.
items.author: Anna Morandi Manzolini

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's mucosa (intestinal metaplasia of the esophagus)
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = columnar (intestinal) metaplasia with goblet cells replacing esophageal squamous epithelium; goblet cells stain blue with Alcian blue pH 2.5; main risk is esophageal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Pautrier microabscesses = intraepidermal clusters of haloed atypical (cerebriform) T cells with minimal spongiosis (epidermotropism) in mycosis fungoides; Munro = neutrophils in the stratum corneum in psoriasis.
items.author: Nooshin Bagherani, Bruce R. Smoller

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic appendectomy
items.caption: Remember: laparoscopic appendectomy uses a triangulated 3-port technique (umbilical camera, suprapubic and left iliac fossa working ports) targeting the right iliac fossa.
items.author: Robystarm07

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Bones of the scapula, ribs and sternum
items.caption: Remember: the scapula has a spine, acromion, coracoid and glenoid; a typical rib has a head, neck, tubercle and shaft with a costal groove; the sternum has manubrium, body and xiphoid process (often bifid).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Deltoid (medial collateral) ligament of the ankle
items.caption: Remember: the deltoid ligament (medial malleolus to navicular, talus and sustentaculum tali) resists eversion, whereas the weaker lateral ligaments (ATFL is the most commonly torn) are injured by inversion.
items.author: Dr. Johannes Sobotta

items.subject: anatomy
items.caption: Remember: the inferior oblique is the only extraocular muscle that does not arise from the orbital apex.
items.author: Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Membranous nephropathy = adult nephrotic syndrome + spike and dome on silver stain + subepithelial deposits on EM + granular IgG/C3 on IF; primary form is anti-PLA2R positive.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Flexor carpi ulnaris
items.caption: Remember: Flexor carpi ulnaris has two heads (medial epicondyle and olecranon/ulna), inserts on pisiform, hamate and 5th metacarpal, and is supplied by the ulnar nerve, the only flexor-compartment wrist flexor with this innervation.
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: in aortic or visceral dissection on 4D flow MRI, the true lumen shows fast, laminar flow and the false lumen shows slower, helical (vortical) flow.
items.author: Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gravid uterus at about the sixth month of gestation with anterior wall and membranes removed, showing fetus, part of placenta and umbilical cord
items.caption: Remember: the fundus reaches the umbilicus at about 20-24 weeks (the sixth month).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Artery (hemostatic) forceps
items.caption: Remember: Hemostat = ring handles + ratchet + slender transversely serrated jaws, used to clamp bleeding vessels.
items.author: Saltanat ebli

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Invasive acral lentiginous melanoma
items.caption: Remember: ALM is the most common melanoma in Indian and dark-skinned patients, occurs on palms, soles and subungual sites, and prognosis is determined by Breslow thickness.
items.author: Xavier-Júnior, José & Munhoz, Tania & Souza, Vinicius & Campos, Eloísa & Stolf, Hamilton & Marques,

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Circle of Willis
items.caption: Remember: Circle of Willis = ACA + ACom + ICA + PCom + PCA (the basilar artery supplies it from behind).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: The axis (C2) is the only vertebra with a dens (odontoid process); its pars interarticularis fracture is the hangman's fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Islet of Langerhans
items.caption: Remember: Islets of Langerhans appear as pale-staining, lightly eosinophilic round clusters in a sea of dark basophilic acini; beta cells (insulin) are most numerous and central, alpha cells (glucagon) peripheral.
items.author: User:Polarlys

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior commissure
items.caption: Remember: the anterior commissure crosses in the lamina terminalis, in front of the fornix columns; its posterior arm connects the anterior temporal lobes and amygdalae, and it lies deep to the uncinate fasciculus and temporal stem.
items.author: Leandro I. Dini, Leonardo M. Vedolin, Debora Bertholdo, Rafael D. Grando, Alessandro Mazzola, Simone

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gall bladder
items.caption: Remember: in laparoscopic cholecystectomy the gallbladder is a pale-bluish pear-shaped sac under the inferior liver edge; always achieve the critical view of safety before clipping.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Maxilla
items.caption: Remember: the orbital floor is mainly the maxilla (with small zygomatic and palatine parts).
items.author: The original uploader was Je at uwo at English Wikipedia .

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Palmar view of dissection of the wrist joint
items.caption: Remember: pisiform and hook of hamate (ulnar side) plus scaphoid and trapezium tubercles (radial side) mark a PALMAR view of the wrist and form the boundaries of the carpal tunnel.
items.author: Anatomist90 , Arabic Derivative: Elbasyouny

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lung buds arising from the laryngotracheal groove of the foregut
items.caption: Remember: Lung buds appear at week 4 as a bifurcation of the laryngotracheal (respiratory) diverticulum of the foregut.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheotomy set
items.caption: Remember: curved flanged tubes with a neck-plate plus tracheal hooks = tracheotomy set.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis)
items.caption: Remember: crescents (parietal epithelial cells + macrophages + fibrin) in >50% of glomeruli = RPGN.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with psammoma body
items.caption: Remember: Psammoma bodies (concentric laminated dystrophic calcification) in a thyroid lesion = papillary carcinoma; think also of PSAMMOMA: Papillary thyroid, Serous ovarian, Meningioma, Mesothelioma, Somatostatinoma.
items.author: Eriugen

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mogen clamp
items.caption: Remember: Mogen clamp = flat slotted metal clamp used for neonatal circumcision, crushing the foreskin while the glans is protected.
items.author: Dan Bollinger

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pudendal nerve with the internal pudendal artery and their branches
items.caption: Remember: the pudendal nerve (S2-S4) leaves through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine, re-enters via the lesser sciatic foramen, and runs in Alcock's canal.
items.author: Norris, Richard Cooper, 1863- Other Authors: Dickinson, Robert Latou, 1861-1950.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gallbladder carcinoma
items.caption: Remember: gallbladder carcinoma is usually adenocarcinoma of the fundus in an older woman with gallstones.
items.author: K C Geetika, Talwar OP

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = replacement of distal esophageal squamous epithelium by columnar epithelium with goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia); it is the precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Renal cell carcinoma
items.caption: Remember: Renal cell carcinoma shows a golden-yellow, variegated cut surface with hemorrhage and necrosis.
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: Crescent = proliferating parietal epithelial cells + macrophages + fibrin in Bowman space; >50% glomeruli with crescents = RPGN.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Superficial dissection of the anterior forearm showing flexor muscles and tendons, radial artery and median nerve
items.caption: Remember: At the wrist the median nerve lies between the tendons of flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus, and the radial artery lies lateral to flexor carpi radialis (the site of the radial pulse).
items.author: George Henry Ford

items.subject: pathology
items.title: CIN 3 with endocervical gland involvement
items.caption: Remember: CIN 3 can extend into endocervical glands (crypt involvement) and still be in situ.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lancelet (amphioxus) circulatory system
items.caption: Remember: the lancelet (amphioxus) has a closed circulation with NO true heart (contractile ventral aorta and bulbilli pump blood), many paired aortic arches, a hepatic portal system, and colourless blood without respiratory pigment.
items.author: Minami Himemiya

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acral lentiginous melanoma in situ
items.caption: Remember: acral lentiginous melanoma in situ shows a lentiginous proliferation of atypical melanocytes (single cells and irregular nests) along the junction and rete ridges of palms, soles or nail unit.
items.author: Xavier-Júnior, José & Munhoz, Tania & Souza, Vinicius & Campos, Eloísa & Stolf, Hamilton & Marques,

items.subject: mrcp-endocrinology
items.title: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
items.caption: Nuclear grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions are the key cytological clues for papillary thyroid carcinoma, and they can be diagnostic even when the architecture is not clearly papillary.

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Acetabular fossa
items.caption: Remember: the acetabular fossa is the non-articular central floor of the acetabulum (ligamentum teres attachment, Haversian fat pad); the lunate surface is the articular horseshoe around it.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Obstetrical forceps (Levret type)
items.caption: Remember: Levret added the pelvic curve to forceps (Chamberlen: cephalic curve only; Smellie: English lock).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with high-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's high-grade dysplasia = marked atypia and loss of polarity that persists to the surface epithelium, with no stromal invasion; low-grade dysplasia shows maturation toward the surface.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior lobe (adenohypophysis pars distalis)
items.caption: Remember: Anterior and intermediate lobes arise from Rathke's pouch (oral ectoderm); the posterior lobe and infundibulum arise from the neuroectoderm of the ventral diencephalon.
items.author: Majumdar S, Farris CL, Kabat BE, Jung DO, Ellsworth BS

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Follicular lymphoma: centrocytes
items.caption: Remember: Follicular lymphoma = t(14;18), BCL2+, CD10+; centrocytes (small cleaved cells) predominate, centroblasts (large, multiple peripheral nucleoli) determine grade.
items.author: Anubha Bajaj

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anatomical dissection carried out personally by Andreas Vesalius, attended by a large group of observers (woodcut, 1543)
items.caption: Remember: Vesalius (Padua, 1543, De humani corporis fabrica) personally dissected human bodies, corrected Galen's animal-based errors, and founded modern anatomy.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Deaver retractor
items.caption: Remember: Deaver retractor = broad, smooth, S-shaped handheld blade to hold back liver, bowel or viscera; Balfour = self-retaining abdominal frame; Richardson = short right-angled blade for the abdominal wall.
items.author: Saltanat

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hurd tonsil dissector and pillar retractor
items.caption: Remember: Hurd dissector and pillar retractor is a double-ended instrument: spatulate end to dissect the tonsil capsule, angled blade to retract the anterior pillar in dissection tonsillectomy.
items.author: This file was contributed to Wikimedia Commons by Missouri Historical Society as part of a cooperati

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Dorsal rami of spinal nerves
items.caption: Remember: each spinal nerve splits into a dorsal ramus (deep back muscles + skin of back, no plexus) and a ventral ramus (anterolateral trunk and limbs, forms plexuses).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Inferior colliculus
items.caption: Remember: Inferior colliculus = auditory relay (brachium to MGB); superior colliculus = visual reflexes (brachium to LGB).
items.author: John A Beal, PhD Dep't. of Cellular Biology & Anatomy, Louisiana State University Health Sciences Ce

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Nodal amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red positivity = salmon-pink in ordinary light and apple-green birefringence in polarized light, due to the cross-beta-pleated sheet of amyloid.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Microsurgical needle holder (Castroviejo-type)
items.caption: Remember: Microsurgical needle holder = spring (looped) handle, pencil grip, fine jaws, often with a lock; gold handles mark fine microsurgical instruments (Castroviejo type).
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gastrocnemius-soleus junction proximal to the Achilles tendon
items.caption: Remember: Tennis leg = medial gastrocnemius tear at the gastrocnemius-soleus aponeurosis junction (Thompson test usually negative); Achilles rupture occurs 2-6 cm above the calcaneus (Thompson positive).
items.author: Ryuta Kinugasa, Toshiaki Oda, Toshihiko Komatsu, V Reggie Edgerton, and Shantanu Sinha

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis
items.caption: Remember: In laparoscopic cholecystectomy, achieve the Critical View of Safety (two and only two structures entering the gallbladder) before clipping the cystic duct and cystic artery, and always retrieve the gallbladder in a bag.
items.author: User:Pschemp

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with high-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's high-grade dysplasia = severe architectural complexity (cribriform, back-to-back glands) plus severe cytologic atypia reaching the surface, with no stromal invasion; invasion into lamina propria or beyond means adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Exophytic adenocarcinoma of the colon
items.caption: Remember: right-sided colon cancer is typically exophytic/fungating and presents with iron-deficiency anemia; left-sided colon cancer is typically annular (apple-core) and presents with obstruction.
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Synovial sarcoma = t(X;18) SS18-SSX, TLE1+, biphasic (spindle + epithelial glands), young adult near the knee, with lung metastases.
items.author: Bjbedke

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy
items.caption: Remember: pressure overload (hypertension, aortic stenosis) causes concentric LVH with parallel sarcomere addition and a small cavity.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Shoulder (pectoral) girdle in superior view, with the clavicles and scapulae rotating about the vertebral center
items.caption: Remember: the pectoral girdle (clavicle + scapula) attaches to the axial skeleton only at the sternoclavicular joint.
items.author: Bobjgalindo

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Cholesterolosis of gallbladder
items.caption: Remember: Strawberry gallbladder = cholesterolosis.
items.author: K C Geetika, Talwar OP

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: the atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process; its body is the dens of C2.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Osteoblastic osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: the diagnostic hallmark of osteosarcoma is osteoid produced directly by malignant cells, irrespective of how much cartilage or fibrous tissue is also present.
items.author: 藤澤孝志

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Graily Hewitt's ordinary long-bladed obstetric forceps
items.caption: Remember: Kielland = sliding lock, minimal pelvic curve, rotation.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Ossicular chain (malleus, incus and stapes)
items.caption: Remember: the ossicular chain runs malleus to incus to stapes, from the tympanic membrane to the oval window.
items.author: Mattia Ferrazzini

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Hepatic amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red + crossed polarized light = apple-green birefringence = amyloid (cross-beta-pleated sheet).
items.author: Tulemo

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Tricuspid valve vegetation (infective endocarditis)
items.caption: Remember: IV drug user + fever + septic pulmonary emboli + TR murmur = right-sided (tricuspid) S.
items.author: Endocarditis_ultrasound.gif : Daisuke Koya, Kazuyuki Shibuya, Ryuichi Kikkawa and Masakazu Haneda. d

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Adult Wilms' tumour (nephroblastoma) with triphasic pattern
items.caption: Remember: Wilms' tumour = triphasic (blastema + epithelial tubules + stroma); rare in adults, where the diagnosis is one of exclusion and the prognosis is worse.
items.author: V Geethamani, V Kusuma, KM Srinivasa Gowda and Monika Lamba Saini.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Colloid nodule
items.caption: Remember: colloid nodule = large colloid-filled macrofollicles with flattened epithelium, no true capsule, often with cracks and fibrosis (part of multinodular goiter).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Severe emphysema
items.caption: Remember: emphysema = permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchiole with wall destruction and NO obvious fibrosis; low FEV1/FVC, high TLC, low DLCO.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: a fasciotomy wound that cannot be closed primarily is covered temporarily (synthetic skin substitute, vessel loop shoelace or NPWT) and then closed late or skin grafted after the swelling resolves.
items.author: User:Mattes

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic hysterectomy
items.caption: Remember: In laparoscopic hysterectomy, the ureter lies beneath the uterine artery ('water under the bridge'), so skeletonize the vessels and keep cautery close to the uterus to avoid ureteric injury.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric adenocarcinoma
items.caption: Remember: a benign gastric ulcer is small, punched-out, with radiating folds.
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with high-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: In Barrett's esophagus, loss of nuclear polarity with marked pleomorphism reaching the surface = high-grade dysplasia (carcinoma in situ); invasion of lamina propria = intramucosal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma, nasal type
items.caption: Remember: Destructive midline nasal lesion + angiocentric necrosis + EBV (EBER+) + CD56+ and cytoplasmic CD3+ = extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma, nasal type.
items.author: Takahara M, Kumai T, Kishibe K, Nagato T, Harabuchi Y

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic groin hernia repair
items.caption: Remember: Three small port scars (umbilical + two lower abdominal) and no groin incision = laparoscopic (TAPP/TEP) groin hernia repair, with mesh in the preperitoneal space covering the myopectineal orifice.
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Small intestinal adenocarcinoma
items.caption: Remember: Small bowel adenocarcinoma is commonest in the duodenum and jejunum, presents as an annular stenosing, ulcerated growth with obstruction or occult bleeding, and is associated with Crohn disease, celiac disease, Lynch syndrome, FAP and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
items.author: Xilin Wu1, Hester Y. S. Cheung, Cliff C. C. Chung, Michael K. W. Li

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Fresh (acute) myocardial infarction of a papillary muscle
items.caption: Remember: Gross MI timeline: 0-12 h nothing visible; 12-24 h dark mottling; 1-3 days mottled with yellow-tan center; 3-7 days hyperemic border with soft yellow center; 2-8 weeks gray-white scar.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Obstetric forceps
items.caption: Remember: obstetric forceps have 4 parts per branch (blade, shank, lock, handle), 2 curves (cephalic and pelvic) and fenestrated blades.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Trachea
items.caption: Remember: the trachea has 16-20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings, begins at C6 (lower border of cricoid), and bifurcates at the carina at the level of the sternal angle (T4-T5).
items.author: Noukayami

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Mandible
items.caption: Remember: the mandible is the only mobile facial bone.
items.author: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg)

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Chronic leg ulcer showing healing by pinch (Reverdin-type) skin grafts
items.caption: Remember: pinch (Reverdin) grafts are small skin pieces placed on a clean granulating bed; each surviving graft becomes an island of epithelium that spreads outward and coalesces with others.
items.author: West, Richard Milbourne

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Femoral triangle
items.caption: Femoral triangle: base = inguinal ligament, lateral = sartorius, medial = adductor longus (medial border).
items.author: Daniel G. Bates

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Superficial lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes of the upper extremity
items.caption: Remember: superficial limb lymphatics follow the superficial veins (cephalic: lateral, basilic: medial) and drain mainly to the axillary nodes.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Weitlaner retractor
items.caption: Remember: Weitlaner = scissor-handled, ratchet-locked, self-retaining retractor with 3 and 4 prongs for superficial wounds; Balfour = abdominal; Finochietto = thoracic.
items.author: MacPiek

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Intrapulmonary lymph node
items.caption: Remember: A subpleural nodule under 1 cm with a marginal sinus, germinal centers, and anthracotic pigment is a benign intrapulmonary lymph node, often found incidentally on CT.
items.author: Yale Rosen from USA

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lingual artery
items.caption: Lingual artery: from external carotid at the tip of the greater cornu of the hyoid, passes DEEP to hyoglossus.
items.author: Dr Johannes Sobotta

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Vermiform appendix
items.caption: Remember: the three taeniae coli converge at the base of the appendix, and this is the guide to finding it at surgery.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.caption: Remember: Post-amputation pain out of proportion, bronze or dusky skin, hemorrhagic bullae, crepitus, and a foul serosanguinous discharge mean gas gangrene.
items.author: Ashashyou

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Ductal carcinoma in situ
items.caption: Remember: E-cadherin positive (membranous) = ductal (DCIS/IDC); E-cadherin negative = lobular (LCIS/ILC).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Pancreatic lipomatosis
items.caption: Remember: Pancreatic lipomatosis = fat infiltration with preserved acini and no fibrosis or inflammation (obesity, T2DM, metabolic syndrome, aging).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: crescent = parietal epithelial cells + macrophages + fibrin in Bowman's space, the hallmark of RPGN.
items.author: Unknown / Public domain

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Foetus in utero
items.caption: Remember: a normal term fetus lies longitudinally in flexed attitude, in cephalic (vertex) presentation in about 95 percent of cases, inside the uterine cavity.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone (greater wing)
items.caption: Remember: Pterion = frontal + parietal + squamous temporal + greater wing of sphenoid (H-shaped), overlying the anterior division of the middle meningeal artery; fracture causes extradural hematoma.
items.author: RosarioVanTulpe created and Teflotax modified it.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Urticaria pigmentosa (cutaneous mastocytosis)
items.caption: Remember: Brown macules that urticate on stroking (Darier sign) in a child = urticaria pigmentosa; biopsy shows dermal mast cells (toluidine blue/Giemsa, CD117, tryptase positive) and basal hyperpigmentation.
items.author: Parag M Tamhankar, Jyoti Suvarna and Chandrahas T Deshmukh

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Normal anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis)
items.caption: Remember: the normal anterior pituitary has a MIXED cell population (acidophils, basophils, chromophobes) in nests with an intact reticulin network.
items.author: Sylvia L. Asa

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Submucous fibroid of the posterior uterine wall
items.caption: Remember: a smooth, pale, firm, broad-based mass bulging into the cavity on hysteroscopy with menorrhagia and infertility is a submucous fibroid.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Malignant cells producing osteoid = osteosarcoma, regardless of the cell type (osteoblastic, chondroblastic, fibroblastic, giant-cell rich); classic in metaphysis of the knee in teens, with Codman triangle and sunburst pattern.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Needle holder
items.caption: Remember: a needle holder has short, stout, flat, cross-hatched jaws (often with a groove or tungsten carbide insert) and a locking ratchet.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: CD10 (neprilysin)
items.caption: Remember: CD10 stains proximal convoluted tubule brush border and glomeruli; clear cell and papillary RCC (proximal tubule origin) are CD10 positive, whereas chromophobe RCC and oncocytoma (distal origin) are CD117 positive and CD10 negative or weak.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Cheatle forceps
items.caption: Remember: Cheatle forceps = long, angled, NON-ratcheted transfer forceps for lifting sterile items from drums.
items.author: Saltanat ebli

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Membranous nephropathy = most common cause of adult nephrotic syndrome in Caucasians.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Costotransverse joints
items.caption: Remember: Costotransverse joints are synovial plane joints between rib tubercle and transverse process (T1-T10).
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Retrieval of the appendix in an Endobag
items.caption: Remember: In laparoscopic appendicectomy, always remove the appendix in an Endobag through the port to prevent port-site infection and tumour seeding.
items.author: Parveen Bhatia, Vinay Sabharwal, Sudhir Kalhan, Suviraj John, Jagpreet S. Deed, and Mukund Khetan

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Adhesions after appendectomy
items.caption: Remember: Previous abdominal surgery (appendectomy, especially for perforation) is the commonest cause of adhesions, and adhesions are the commonest cause of small bowel obstruction in adults.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Left anterolateral (resuscitative) thoracotomy through the 4th or 5th intercostal space with a Finochietto rib retractor
items.caption: Remember: Resuscitative thoracotomy is a left anterolateral incision in the 4th/5th intercostal space at the nipple level, and the Finochietto retractor handle points down toward the bed (axilla/bed side) so a clamshell extension remains possible.
items.author: Cothren and Moore; licensee BioMed Central Ltd.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red positive, apple-green birefringence under polarized light = amyloid (beta-pleated sheet); AL type is associated with myeloma and macroglossia.
items.author: Ed Uthman, MD

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Term gravid uterus with a flexed fetus in longitudinal lie, anterior wall reflected
items.caption: Remember: at term the normal fetus lies in a longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, with full flexion (vertex, occipitoanterior commonest), the attitude of universal flexion.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Placenta previa
items.caption: Remember: painless, recurrent, bright red bleeding in the third trimester means placenta previa until proven otherwise.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Humerus
items.caption: Remember: Humerus = largest bone of the upper limb; spherical head proximally, radial nerve in the spiral groove of the shaft, axillary nerve at the surgical neck, ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle.
items.author: Doctor Jana

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gravid uterus in situ after reflection of the abdominal wall
items.caption: Remember: the uterus becomes an abdominal organ after about 12 weeks and its fundus reaches the xiphisternum at about 36 weeks.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Skin-grafting scissors
items.caption: Remember: Skin-grafting scissors have fine, long, curved, pointed blades for atraumatic trimming of thin grafts; heavy blunt-tipped Mayo scissors cut fascia.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Liston bone cutting forceps (curved)
items.caption: Remember: Liston bone cutting forceps = long handles, spring, sharp cutting blades (straight or curved) used to trim bone ends, e.g., after amputation; Luer = nibbling cups.
items.author: AfroBrazilian

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Traumatic myocardial injury (contusion) with ruptured intercalated discs
items.caption: Remember: intercalated discs are the mechanical weak point of cardiac muscle.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gomco clamp
items.caption: Remember: Gomco = metal base plate + bell + yoke arm tightened by a screw (crush, then cut).
items.author: Dan Bollinger

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: Hydrocele of canal of Nuck = female equivalent of encysted hydrocele of the cord, a translucent inguinal/labial cyst along the round ligament.
items.author: Wang, L., Maejima, T., Fukahori, S. et al.

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Deep abdominal dissection showing the great arteries and veins with the kidneys
items.caption: Remember: deep abdominal dissection = aorta (left of midline), IVC (right of midline) and kidneys against the posterior abdominal wall, with the renal vessels at the hila (renal vein anterior to artery).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Circle of Willis
items.caption: Remember: Circle of Willis = ACA + anterior communicating + ICA + posterior communicating + PCA (from basilar bifurcation).
items.author: John Campbell

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Telangiectatic osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: telangiectatic osteosarcoma mimics aneurysmal bone cyst (fluid-fluid levels) but shows highly pleomorphic malignant cells in the septa; sample the septa thoroughly.
items.author: 藤澤孝志

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile cardiac amyloidosis (wild-type transthyretin)
items.caption: Remember: elderly man + restrictive cardiomyopathy + low-voltage ECG with thick walls + no monoclonal protein = wild-type ATTR (senile) cardiac amyloidosis.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Germinal center of a secondary lymphoid follicle
items.caption: Remember: pale germinal center inside a dark-rimmed cortical nodule = secondary follicle (B-cell activation).
items.author: Gleiberg

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Malignant melanoma in situ
items.caption: Remember: Melanoma in situ shows atypical melanocytes in nests and single cells at all epidermal levels (pagetoid spread) with no dermal invasion; confirm with S100, SOX10, and Melan-A.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Ridged band of the prepuce
items.caption: Remember: the ridged band is the corrugated mucocutaneous zone of the inner foreskin, rich in Meissner-type fine-touch corpuscles.
items.author: 57ukab

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Melanoma brain metastasis
items.caption: Remember: brown-black pigmented epithelioid cells in the brain plus T1-hyperintense hemorrhagic lesion = melanoma metastasis (S100, SOX10, HMB-45, Melan-A positive); melanoma is the most brain-avid metastasis per frequency.
items.author: Jensflorian

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Orbit showing the extraocular muscles with their motor nerves (oculomotor, trochlear and abducens)
items.caption: Remember: LR6 SO4 AO3.
items.author: Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Plain (uncuffed) tracheostomy tube
items.caption: Remember: plain (uncuffed) tracheostomy tube = flange with tape slots, no cuff or pilot balloon.
items.author: Tenbergen

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Deep plane facelift with SMAS elevation and fixation suture placement
items.caption: Remember: The SMAS is the layer continuous with the platysma, parotid fascia and temporoparietal fascia; facelifts reposition it, and the facial nerve branches lie deep to it.
items.author: Richard Balikian MD

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric hyperplastic polyp
items.caption: Remember: Gastric hyperplastic polyp = elongated, tortuous, cystic foveolae + edematous inflamed stroma, in a background of chronic gastritis (H.
items.author: Gabriel M. Groisman, Roman Depsames, Baruch Ovadia and Alona Meir

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Open (Hasson) entry technique
items.caption: Remember: Hasson = open entry under direct vision with a blunt cannula and stay sutures.
items.author: Melmd2020

items.subject: mrcp-respiratory
items.caption: Mature teratoma is the most common benign mediastinal germ cell tumour, and the presence of fat, calcification and hair within a mediastinal mass should prompt this diagnosis.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Chorangiosis
items.caption: Remember: chorangiosis = at least 10 villi with at least 10 capillaries each in at least 3 areas (diffuse, within villi), seen in diabetes and chronic hypoxia.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acute chorioamnionitis
items.caption: Remember: neutrophils in chorion/amnion = acute chorioamnionitis (maternal response); neutrophils in cord/chorionic plate vessels, or fibrin thrombi = fetal inflammatory response (funisitis/chorionic vasculitis).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Curved artery forceps (mosquito/Halsted type)
items.caption: Remember: Artery forceps = ratcheted, box-lock, serrated, non-toothed jaws that clamp vessels; mosquito forceps are the smaller, finer version used in delicate ENT and paediatric surgery.
items.author: Netha Hussain

items.subject: pathology
items.title: High-grade osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Osteosarcoma = malignant cells producing osteoid (pink, glassy, lace-like matrix); adolescent metaphysis (distal femur/proximal tibia), raised ALP, Codman triangle, sunburst pattern, lung metastases.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Wilms' tumor = triphasic (blastema + stroma + epithelial tubules/abortive glomeruli); the most common pediatric renal tumor, with a good prognosis.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Sponge holding forceps
items.caption: Remember: Sponge holding forceps (Rampley's) have open, ring-shaped, serrated jaws for holding swabs.
items.author: Saltanat

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lumbar plexus
items.caption: Remember: Lumbar plexus = anterior rami L1-L4 (plus T12 contribution), lying within psoas major; branches: Iliohypogastric, Ilioinguinal, Genitofemoral, Lateral femoral cutaneous, Obturator, Femoral.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axial skeleton
items.caption: Remember: Axial skeleton = 80 bones (skull, hyoid, ossicles, vertebral column, ribs, sternum); appendicular = 126 bones (girdles plus limbs).
items.author: Anatomography is provided by DBCLS

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Temporal bone
items.caption: Remember: The temporal bone carries the zygomatic process, external acoustic meatus, mastoid process and styloid process; its squamous part forms part of the pterion (H-shaped junction with the sphenoid, frontal and parietal bones).
items.author: Welleschik, adapted from public domain source

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Negri bodies = eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in hippocampal pyramidal neurons and cerebellar Purkinje cells = pathognomonic of rabies (composed of viral nucleoprotein); absent in about 20-30% of cases.
items.author: Content Provider(s): CDC/Dr. Daniel P. Perl

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Roman forceps with fine-toothed hollow jaws
items.caption: Remember: Roman forceps have a scissor-type pivot (crossed arms) with fine-toothed hollow jaws to grip foreign bodies and tissue, unlike a speculum (valves), catheter (hollow tube) or lever (single shaft).
items.author: Marie-Lan Nguyen (2011)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: High-grade osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: osteosarcoma = malignant cells producing osteoid (pink, glassy, lace-like).
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Acetabular notch
items.caption: Remember: the acetabular notch is the inferior gap in the acetabular rim, bridged by the transverse acetabular ligament, and the acetabular branch of the obturator artery enters through it.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Epithelioid leiomyosarcoma of the uterus
