items.caption: Remember: epithelioid smooth muscle tumor of the uterus is called malignant with 2 of 3 features: moderate to severe atypia, tumor cell necrosis, and 4 or more mitoses per 10 HPF (versus 10 or more for the spindle cell type).
items.author: Luke King1, Radhika P Gogoi, Christopher Hummel, Zongming Chen and Ashlee Smith

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Displaced intra-articular distal radius fracture
items.caption: Remember: Intra-articular distal radius fracture with articular step-off over 2 mm needs anatomical reduction and fixation to prevent post-traumatic arthritis; check radial height, inclination and volar tilt.
items.author: Curtishand

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Neural crest
items.caption: Remember: The neural crest arises at the lateral margins of the neural folds at the neuroectoderm-surface ectoderm junction.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1) articulated with the axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: the atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process.
items.author: MAKY.OREL

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Graves' disease
items.caption: Remember: Graves' disease = diffuse hyperplasia with tall columnar cells, papillae lacking fibrovascular cores, and scalloped pale colloid with clear marginal vacuoles; nuclei remain bland, unlike papillary carcinoma.
items.author: LiVolsi VA and Baloch ZW

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Postmortem autolysis of thyroid parenchyma
items.caption: Remember: Epithelial cells sloughed into the lumen of intact organs, with no inflammation, is autolysis (an autopsy artifact), not disease.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic (rapidly progressive) glomerulonephritis with fibrocellular crescent
items.caption: Remember: crescent = proliferation of parietal epithelial cells plus macrophages in Bowman's space, with fibrin as the trigger.
items.author: Arunachalam Ramaswami, Thiraviam Kandaswamy, Tholappan Rajendran, Kizhake Pisharam Jeyakrishnan, Hla

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.caption: Remember: crepitus + pain out of proportion + dusky skin + foul serosanguinous discharge in a stump within 1-3 days = gas gangrene (Clostridium perfringens).
items.author: Ashashyou

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Needle holder (left) and straight hemostat (right)
items.caption: Remember: Needle holder = short, stout jaws with a central groove and crosshatching to grip the needle.
items.author: Ricce

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgical skin staple remover
items.caption: Remember: A staple remover looks like scissors with plastic rings but does not cut.
items.author: Raimond Spekking

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
items.caption: Remember: Single-incision laparoscopic cholecystectomy uses a multichannel umbilical port (e.g., TriPort); the gallbladder is extracted through the umbilicus, and the critical view of safety is mandatory before clipping.
items.author: Roland Raakow and Dietmar A. Jacob

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Colles fracture with ulnar styloid fracture
items.caption: Remember: Colles = dorsal displacement of the distal radius (dinner-fork deformity), extra-articular, within 2.5 cm of the joint, often with ulnar styloid avulsion.
items.author: Lucien Monfils

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lumbar sympathetic trunk with its ganglia
items.caption: Remember: the lumbar sympathetic trunk lies on the medial psoas, anterolateral to the vertebral bodies; bilateral injury at L1-L3 causes anejaculation with preserved erection.
items.author: George Henry Ford (1809-1876)

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Spleen
items.caption: Remember: the spleen is the dark maroon, intraperitoneal organ under the left diaphragm (ribs 9-11) and the most commonly injured organ in blunt abdominal trauma.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic malignant melanoma of the myocardium
items.caption: Remember: Melanoma is the tumour with the highest propensity to metastasise to the heart.
items.author: Student BSMU

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with low-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: in Barrett's esophagus, dysplasia (not metaplasia) predicts cancer risk.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Right distal radius and ulna, anterior view
items.caption: Remember: the radius is the lateral (thumb side) forearm bone with a wide distal end that articulates with the scaphoid and lunate, while the ulna's distal head is excluded from the wrist joint by the articular disc.
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: the axis (C2) has the dens, the largest bifid spinous process of the upper cervical spine, and a pars interarticularis whose bilateral fracture gives hangman's fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Obstetrical forceps of Haighton
items.caption: Remember: Haighton's forceps has a single bulbous wooden handle with scissor-like fenestrated blade loops, whereas Kielland has a sliding lock, Simpson a long pelvic curve and Smellie an English lock with two handles.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: High-grade osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Osteosarcoma = malignant cells making osteoid (pink, glassy, homogeneous matrix).
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gossypiboma (retained surgical sponge)
items.caption: Remember: Gossypiboma = retained surgical sponge (Latin gossypium = cotton, Swahili boma = place of concealment).
items.author: I, the copyright holder of this work, hereby publish it under the following license:

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Dental extracting forceps (titanium-coated)
items.caption: Remember: Dental extraction forceps have a hinge, beaks that grip the tooth at the cervical margin, and handles set at an angle to the beaks.
items.author: Bszsurgico

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Wound dehiscence following inguinal hernia repair
items.caption: Remember: Wound dehiscence typically occurs on postoperative days 5 to 10; a serosanguinous discharge ('pink fluid sign') often precedes fascial dehiscence.
items.author: User:Phoenix119

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Left complete (inguinoscrotal) indirect inguinal hernia
items.caption: Remember: a scrotal swelling where you cannot get above it is an inguinal hernia (inguinoscrotal); a hydrocele allows you to get above it.
items.author: Amadalvarez

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Needle holder
items.caption: Remember: A needle holder has short, stout jaws with a crosshatched or serrated gripping surface and a ratchet lock.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Radius and ulna
items.caption: Remember: the radius is narrow proximally and wide distally, while the ulna is wide proximally (olecranon) and narrow distally.
items.author: Hellerhoff

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome) with crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: Linear IgG on IF + crescents + hemoptysis = anti-GBM (Goodpasture), type II hypersensitivity against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Circle of Willis
items.caption: Remember: Circle of Willis = ACA + AComA + ICA + PComA + PCA (with basilar artery at the base).
items.author: John Campbell

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HPV effect)
items.caption: Remember: LSIL = koilocytes (nuclear enlargement 3x, hyperchromasia, raisinoid irregular contours, binucleation, perinuclear halo) in mature squamous cells with a low N:C ratio; HSIL = immature basaloid cells with a high N:C ratio.
items.author: Photomicrograph by Ed Uthman, MD. 20 July 2006 Euthman 20:24, 29 November 2006 (UTC)

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Collin tongue forceps
items.caption: Remember: Collin tongue forceps have two large oval fenestrated, serrated rings to pull the tongue forward in airway obstruction (glossoptosis) or oral surgery.
items.author: Citizen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gravid uterus at term
items.caption: Remember: the uterus is a pelvic organ that becomes abdominal after about 12 weeks.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: the axis (C2) is the only vertebra with a dens (odontoid process); bilateral pars fractures of C2 = hangman's fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Smellie's leather wrapped forceps
items.caption: Remember: Smellie = English lock + pelvic curve + leather-wrapped blades.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: ROSAH syndrome
items.caption: Remember: ROSAH = Retinal dystrophy, Optic nerve oedema, Splenomegaly, Anhidrosis, Headache; autosomal dominant ALPK1 (p.Thr237Met) gain-of-function autoinflammatory disease, also with arthritis, short dental roots and basal ganglia mineralisation.
items.author: Kozycki et al.

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Brachial plexus
items.caption: Remember: Brachial plexus = Roots, Trunks, Divisions, Cords, Branches (C5-T1); cords lie behind pectoralis minor and are named by their relation to the axillary artery.
items.author: Anatomist90

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mixter (right angle) clamp
items.caption: Remember: A right angle (Mixter/Lahey) clamp has jaws bent at about 90 degrees.
items.author: Saltanat ebli

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pericytes
items.caption: Remember: Pericytes lie on the abluminal side of the endothelium, embedded in the shared basement membrane.
items.author: Seiji Miyata

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Distal radius and ulna of the right forearm (posterior view)
items.caption: Remember: the radius is the wrist-forming bone and bears Lister's dorsal tubercle, while the ulnar head and styloid lie medially and are separated from the carpus by the articular disc.
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: mrcp-neurology
items.title: Intracranial epidermoid cyst
items.caption: Epidermoid cysts restrict diffusion on DWI and do not enhance with gadolinium, which helps distinguish them from vestibular schwannoma and meningioma.

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Capitate bone
items.caption: Remember: Capitate = largest carpal bone, centre of the distal row, articulates with the base of the 3rd metacarpal; its proximal pole has retrograde blood supply, so waist fractures risk avascular necrosis.
items.author: Photo is by Brian C. Goss

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Deaver retractor
items.caption: Remember: Deaver = broad, curved, handheld retractor for retracting organs (liver, bowel) deep in the abdomen; Balfour = self-retaining; Morris = flat blade with right-angled lip; Langenbeck = small right-angled blade for superficial wounds.
items.author: Saltanat ebli

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas and axis (C1 and C2)
items.caption: Remember: the atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process.
items.author: MAKY.OREL

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: The sphenoid (bat-shaped) is the only bone that touches all other cranial bones; its greater wing forms the posterior lateral orbital wall and part of the pterion.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Leiomyosarcoma of the uterus
items.caption: Remember: Uterine leiomyosarcoma = spindle cells with cigar-shaped atypical nuclei + atypical mitoses + tumor cell necrosis; hallmark criteria are atypia, necrosis and mitoses of 10 or more per 10 HPF; hematogenous spread to the lung.
items.author: Eiji Kobayashi, Takuhei Yokoyama, Satoshi Nakagawa, Shinya Matsuzaki, Toshihiro Kimura, Yutaka Ueda,

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with low-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's low-grade dysplasia = pseudostratified, hyperchromatic pencil-shaped nuclei with preserved polarity and no marked architectural complexity; Barrett's itself is columnar metaplasia with goblet cells and carries a risk of adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Superficial spreading melanoma
items.caption: Remember: superficial spreading melanoma = most common subtype, large confluent junctional nests with pagetoid spread, radial growth phase first, Breslow thickness is the key prognostic factor.
items.author: Juliana Casagrande Tavoloni Braga, Mariana Petaccia Macedo, Clovis Pinto, João Duprat, Maria Dirlei

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Nodular melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Nodular melanoma = vertical growth phase from the start, no radial growth component, thick at diagnosis (poor prognosis).
items.author: Image courtesy of Dr. Ahmet Cemil Kaur Article authors: Zekayi Kutlubay, Burhan Engin, Server Serdar

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheostomy tube set
items.caption: Remember: a tracheostomy tube set = outer cannula with neck flange and cuff + removable inner cannula (cleaned to prevent crusting) + obturator for insertion (removed once the tube is placed).
items.author: Klaus D. Peter, Wiehl, Germany Diese Datei aus meinem Archiv habe ich unter der „ Creative-Commons -

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Complete disruption of the right bronchus intermedius (tracheobronchial injury)
items.caption: Remember: blunt tracheobronchial injury is typically within 2.5 cm of the carina, more often on the right.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Malignant melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Heavily pigmented epithelioid cells with melanin obscuring nuclei = melanoma.
items.author: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical College

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Phrenic nerve
items.caption: Remember: the phrenic nerve (C3-5) runs ANTERIOR to the lung root on the pericardium with the pericardiacophrenic vessels, whereas the vagus runs POSTERIOR to the lung root.
items.author: Dr Johannes Sobotta

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Two-piece colostomy bag (pouch)
items.caption: Remember: a two-piece stoma system has a separate adhesive flange and a detachable pouch, so the pouch can be changed without stripping peristomal skin.
items.author: Original uploader was DCwom at en.wikipedia

items.subject: pathology
items.caption: Remember: Bowen disease (SCC in situ) = full-thickness keratinocyte atypia with an intact basement membrane.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Trapezius
items.caption: Trapezius: occiput, ligamentum nuchae, and C7-T12 spines to the lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, and scapular spine.
items.author: Frederick Henry Gerrish (1845-1920)

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Transverse section of the thorax showing the contents of the middle and posterior mediastinum
items.caption: Remember: the middle mediastinum contains the pericardium, heart, roots of the great vessels, main bronchi, phrenic nerves and hilar structures.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic bilateral salpingectomy
items.caption: Remember: Opportunistic bilateral salpingectomy gives permanent sterilization and lowers the risk of high-grade serous ovarian cancer, because the fimbrial end of the tube is the site of origin of many such cancers.
items.author: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Zachary Nordheim

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Curved artery forceps (Negus)
items.caption: Remember: Negus = long, curved-tip artery forceps for deep ENT sites (tonsillar fossa, throat); Mosquito = short, fine; Kocher = 1-in-2 teeth; Allis = fenestrated tissue grasper.
items.author: Netha Hussain

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Fenestra vestibuli (oval window)
items.caption: Remember: the oval window (fenestra vestibuli) lies above the promontory and holds the stapes footplate, while the round window lies below and behind the promontory.
items.author: Welleschik

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Nodular hyperplasia of the thyroid
items.caption: Remember: multinodular goiter = variably sized colloid-filled follicles with flat epithelium, hemorrhage, cystic change and fibrosis, without a complete capsule or nuclear atypia.
items.author: Ji Young Lee, Hee-Sung Song, , Jae Hyuck Choi, Chang Lim Hyun, Sang Ah Lee, Joon-Hyouk Choi and Seok

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gonadotrophs
items.caption: Remember: Basophils of the anterior pituitary = B-FLAT (FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH); they stain blue-violet and are PAS positive.
items.author: Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Pantaloon inguinal hernia
items.caption: Remember: Pantaloon hernia = direct + indirect sacs straddling the inferior epigastric vessels (like a pair of trousers).
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: Crescent = parietal epithelial cell and macrophage proliferation plus fibrin in Bowman's space (more than 50% of glomeruli) = RPGN.
items.author: Arunachalam Ramaswami, Thiraviam Kandaswamy, Tholappan Rajendran, Kizhake Pisharam Jeyakrishnan, Hla

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Roman surgical instruments (forceps and related tools) found at Pompeii
items.caption: Roman surgical kits from Pompeii (79 CE) include forceps, scalpels, catheters and screw-mechanism specula, now in the National Museum of Naples.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic appendectomy
items.caption: Remember: three small incisions (umbilical camera port, suprapubic port, left iliac fossa port) after right iliac fossa pain = laparoscopic appendectomy; open = single McBurney/gridiron incision.
items.author: KAOSkonfused

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mayo-Hegar (Heger) needle holder
items.caption: Remember: A needle holder has short, stout jaws with a central groove (often crosshatched) and a ratchet, and is used to grip the needle about one-third to halfway from the swage.
items.author: Slashatdot

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Totally extraperitoneal (TEP) inguinal hernia repair with preperitoneal mesh placement
items.caption: Remember: in TEP, mesh lies in the preperitoneal space (between transversalis fascia and peritoneum) over the myopectineal orifice, and the peritoneal cavity is never entered.
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Fibrous dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: fibrous dysplasia = Chinese-character woven bone trabeculae without osteoblastic rimming in a fibrous stroma, ground-glass radiograph, GNAS mutation; McCune-Albright = polyostotic FD + café-au-lait spots + precocious puberty.
items.author: Marvin 101

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Senile cardiac amyloidosis = wild-type transthyretin; Congo red shows apple-green birefringence; elderly man with HFpEF, thick walls and low-voltage ECG; lipofuscin coexists as an age-related pigment.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.caption: Remember: Gas in soft tissue on X-ray plus severe pain, crepitus, brownish foul discharge and toxemia after surgery in a diabetic = clostridial gas gangrene: urgent debridement or amputation, penicillin plus clindamycin.
items.author: Ashashyou

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Slotted Pennington forceps
items.caption: Remember: Slotted Pennington forceps have a triangular, open-slotted tip that lets the blade pass through the slot, which is why it is used in circumcision and to grasp broad areas of tissue.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. Pascal666 assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Stromal fibrosis of the breast
items.caption: Remember: Stromal fibrosis = dense, hypocellular, hyalinized collagen with entrapped fat and atrophic ducts; a benign mimic of carcinoma on imaging and palpation, with no increased cancer risk.
items.author: Nassar, Lara; Baassiri, Amro; Salah, Fatima; Barakat, Andrew; Najem, Elie; Boulos, Fouad; Berjawi, G

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: Atlas (C1) = ring-shaped vertebra with no body and no spinous process; its body is the dens of C2.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Adrenal venous congestion due to circulatory failure
items.caption: Remember: Adrenal congestion = dilated sinusoids with intact cortical cells (passive, from heart failure/shock); Waterhouse-Friderichsen = massive hemorrhage with destruction of the gland (meningococcemia/DIC).
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus with low-grade dysplasia
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus is columnar (intestinal) metaplasia replacing squamous epithelium due to chronic GERD; dysplasia (low vs high grade) is the best marker of progression to adenocarcinoma, and nuclear stratification extending to the surface favors higher grade.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
items.caption: Remember: Canal of Nuck = female processus vaginalis accompanying the round ligament; its hydrocele presents as a translucent, non-reducible inguinal or labial swelling and is treated by excision with high ligation.
items.author: Nakamura, K., Higashiguchi, T., Chikaishi, Y. et al.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Uveal (choroidal) melanoma
items.caption: Remember: the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults is uveal (choroidal) melanoma; it spreads hematogenously to the liver, and monosomy 3 and BAP1 loss predict poor prognosis.
items.author: Radioxoma

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: Splenosis = multiple, scattered, dark-maroon peritoneal nodules after splenic trauma or splenectomy.
items.author: Bernhard138

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Superficial spreading melanoma in situ
items.caption: Remember: superficial spreading melanoma in situ shows pagetoid, single and nested atypical melanocytes confined to the epidermis (Breslow 0); dermoscopy shows a broadened atypical network, and RCM shows ringed and disrupted DEJ patterns.
items.author: Juliana Casagrande Tavoloni Braga, Mariana Petaccia Macedo, Clovis Pinto, João Duprat, Maria Dirlei

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Sigmoid colon diverticulum
items.caption: Remember: colonic diverticula are false (pseudo) diverticula, mucosa and submucosa herniating through the muscularis at vasa recta entry points, most common in the sigmoid colon.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: anatomy
items.caption: Remember: SMA arises at L1 behind the pancreatic neck, supplies the midgut (distal duodenum to proximal 2/3 transverse colon); embolism in AF gives pain out of proportion to findings.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Lipoma of the spermatic cord (inguinal canal lipoma)
items.caption: Remember: Cord lipoma is the most common tumour of the spermatic cord and a classic hernia mimic.
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic melanoma
items.caption: Remember: A node replaced by sheets of tumour with brown-black pigment after a pigmented skin lesion is metastatic melanoma (S100, SOX10, HMB-45, Melan-A positive).
items.author: Gabriel Caponetti

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Microsurgical needle holder with ratchet lock
items.caption: Remember: Gold-coloured handles or jaws with a fine, short serrated grip and a ratchet lock indicate a needle holder (tungsten carbide or titanium nitride insert); micro needle holders are used with 9-0 to 11-0 sutures.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: The sphenoid is the keystone of the skull base, articulating with 12 bones; it bears the pterygoid processes and transmits CN II, III, IV, V1, V2, V3 and VI via its foramina and fissures.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red positive amyloid shows apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Sigmoid diverticulosis
items.caption: Remember: sigmoid colon diverticula are false (pulsion) diverticula at vasa recta entry points, caused by a low-fibre diet and high intraluminal pressure; the rectum is spared.
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Compression forceps (applicator) for Yasargil aneurysm clips
items.caption: Remember: Yasargil clips are applied with a bayonet-shaped, spring-handled applicator that opens the clip, and the bayonet shaft keeps the surgeon's hand out of the microscope view during aneurysm clipping.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Trapezoid bone
items.caption: Remember: Trapezoid = smallest bone of the distal carpal row, articulates with the 2nd metacarpal, scaphoid, trapezium and capitate.
items.author: Photo is by Brian C. Goss

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: The atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process; it is a ring with lateral masses that carries the skull and permits nodding (flexion-extension).
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Cartilaginous precursors of the pelvic bones (hyaline cartilage models)
items.caption: Remember: Pelvic bones (like long bones and vertebrae) form by endochondral ossification from hyaline cartilage models.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Cerebellum with brainstem and cranial nerves
items.caption: Remember: the cerebellum has fine parallel transverse folia (the 'arbor vitae' on section) and lies in the posterior cranial fossa.
items.author: John Campbell

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Subchorionic intervillositis
items.caption: Remember: neutrophils in subchorionic fibrin (Langhans fibrinoid layer) or intervillous space = acute subchorionic intervillositis/placentitis, usually from ascending infection, associated with chorioamnionitis and preterm labor.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Fresh (acute) myocardial infarction of the papillary muscle
items.caption: Remember: gross change in MI appears only after 12-24 h (dark mottling), then pale yellow-tan with a hyperaemic border at 3-7 days, and a white scar after weeks.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Cervical stump after supracervical hysterectomy
items.caption: Remember: Supracervical (subtotal) hysterectomy leaves a white coagulated cervical stump with the endocervical canal at its center, and the patient still needs cervical screening.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic Ewing sarcoma
items.caption: Ewing sarcoma: small blue round cells, PAS-positive and diastase-sensitive (glycogen), CD99 and FLI1 positive, t(11;22) EWSR1-FLI1; lung is the commonest metastatic site.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pars distalis of the anterior pituitary gland
items.caption: Remember: the pars distalis shows a mixed population of acidophils (GH, PRL), basophils (ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH) and chromophobes in cords with sinusoids; the pars nervosa shows axons and Herring bodies.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Annular (napkin-ring) adenocarcinoma of the colon
items.caption: Remember: left-sided colon cancer = annular 'napkin-ring' constricting lesion (obstruction, pencil-thin stools); right-sided = polypoid fungating mass (iron deficiency anemia).
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Superior view of the right orbit after removal of the orbital roof
items.caption: Remember: in a superior view of the orbit, the superior oblique runs along the superomedial wall to the trochlea.
items.author: Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C
items.caption: Remember: HCV cirrhosis shows fibrous septa with chronic lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, often with portal lymphoid aggregates and mild steatosis.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acute graft-versus-host disease of the skin
items.caption: Remember: Acute skin GVHD is graded I-IV: I basal vacuolization, II dyskeratotic bodies, III subepidermal cleft, IV complete epidermal separation (TEN-like).
items.author: Sakhila Ghimire, Daniela Weber, Emily Mavin,Xiao nong Wang,Anne Mary Dickinson and Ernst Holler1

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Petrous part of the temporal bone
items.caption: Remember: the petrous temporal bone is the densest bone in the body.
items.author: DrKellyBlevins

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pituitary gland
items.caption: Remember: the pituitary lies in the sella turcica, directly above the sphenoid sinus and below the optic chiasma, so a pituitary adenoma causes bitemporal hemianopia and is removed by the transsphenoidal route.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. Jomegat assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Brachial plexus
items.caption: Remember: Brachial plexus = Roots (C5-T1), Trunks, Divisions, Cords, Branches; it passes between anterior and middle scalenes and the cords surround the axillary artery.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Retractor
items.caption: Remember: A retractor is a single flat blade with a bent or hooked end that holds back soft tissue (muscle, skin) to expose the operative field.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: Atlas (C1) has no body or spinous process; Axis (C2) has the dens and is the pivot for head rotation.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Articulated bony pelvis
items.caption: Remember: the bony pelvis = two hip bones (ilium + ischium + pubis, fusing at the acetabulum) + sacrum + coccyx.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Floor of the fourth ventricle (rhomboid fossa)
items.caption: Remember: the facial colliculus (facial fibres looping over the abducens nucleus) and the striae medullares (pons-medulla border) are the landmarks of the rhomboid fossa.
items.author: Christian Brogna, José Pedro Lavrador, Hussein Shaaban Kandeel, Ahmad Beyh, Eduardo C. Ribas, France

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Shoulder (pectoral) girdle, superior view
items.caption: Remember: the pectoral (shoulder) girdle = clavicle + scapula; its only bony attachment to the axial skeleton is the sternoclavicular joint, which allows wide mobility.
items.author: Bobjgalindo

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic malignant melanoma
items.caption: Brown-black granular pigment in atypical epithelioid cells in a brain mass = metastatic melanoma (S-100, SOX10, HMB-45 positive; T1 hyperintense, hemorrhagic).
items.author: Jensflorian

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic melanoma in the liver
items.caption: Remember: coarse black-brown pigment plus malignant cells in the liver means metastatic melanoma.
items.author: Radioxoma

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Bronchial stenosis at the site of surgical repair
items.caption: Remember: after tracheobronchial repair, a fixed narrowing at the anastomosis on 3D CT or virtual bronchoscopy means post-surgical stenosis from granulation or fibrosis.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: anatomy
items.caption: Remember: transverse lie with shoulder presentation means the pelvic inlet is empty of a fetal pole and the presenting part is high.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Magill catheter introducing forceps
items.caption: Remember: Magill forceps are angled so the hand does not obstruct the view during laryngoscopy.
items.author: AfroBrazilian

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic melanoma invading pancreatic tissue
items.caption: Remember: Melanoma is the great mimicker; large epithelioid cells with macronucleoli and intranuclear pseudoinclusions in an unexpected site should prompt S100/SOX10/HMB-45 staining.
items.author: Richard Lee, M.D., Ph.D., National Cancer Institute (NCI)

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior inferior iliac spine
items.caption: Remember: AIIS = straight head of rectus femoris (and iliofemoral ligament); ASIS = sartorius and inguinal ligament.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Talocalcaneal and talocalcaneonavicular articulations
items.caption: Remember: Removing the talus exposes the talocalcaneonavicular socket, formed by the navicular, the calcaneal facets and the plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Peritoneal cavity
items.caption: Remember: the peritoneal cavity is a closed sac in males, and in females it is open via the uterine tubes.
items.author: Sheldahl

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Fournier gangrene
items.caption: Remember: Fournier gangrene is polymicrobial necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum and genitalia, commonly in diabetics.
items.author: Mohammd Kazem Moslemi, Mohammad Ali Sadighi Gilani, Ali Akbar Moslemi and Ali Arabshahi

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Classical chordoma
items.caption: Remember: Chordoma = physaliphorous (bubbly) cells in myxoid matrix, midline sacrococcygeal or clival mass, brachyury positive, notochord remnant origin.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Adrenal cortical necrosis
items.caption: Remember: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome = meningococcemia + DIC + bilateral adrenal hemorrhage and cortical necrosis leading to acute adrenal crisis.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Circle of Willis
items.caption: Remember: the Circle of Willis is formed by the anterior communicating, both anterior cerebral, both internal carotid, both posterior communicating and both posterior cerebral arteries.
items.author: The original uploader was MBq at German Wikipedia .

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mixter (right angle) clamp
items.caption: Remember: Right angle (Mixter/Lahey) clamp = 90-degree jaw bend, used to pass a ligature behind a vessel or duct (cystic artery, intercostal vessels, PDA).
items.author: Saltanat ebli

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Pathologically deformed pelvis with angular distortion
items.caption: Remember: osteomalacia or rickets softens the pelvis, giving a triradiate (trefoil) inlet, a forward-pushed promontory, a beaked pubis and a narrow pubic arch, so cephalopelvic disproportion and obstructed labour follow.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Microsurgical needle holder
items.caption: Remember: a needle holder has short jaws with a tungsten carbide insert and a box-lock, whereas a hemostat has long serrated jaws with a ratchet and forceps are spring-type.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Small intestinal adenocarcinoma
items.caption: Remember: A short, napkin-ring constricting lesion in the small bowel of an older adult with occult bleeding and obstruction is adenocarcinoma until proven otherwise; small bowel adenocarcinoma is commonest in the duodenum and is associated with Crohn disease, celiac disease and polyposis syndromes.
items.author: Xilin Wu1, Hester Y. S. Cheung, Cliff C. C. Chung, Michael K. W. Li

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
items.caption: Remember: laparoscopic cholecystectomy = 4 ports: umbilical (camera), epigastric (main working), and two right-sided 5 mm ports (mid-clavicular and anterior axillary) for gallbladder retraction.
items.author: Kim

items.subject: mrcp-gastroenterology
items.title: Stomach
items.caption: Bilateral solid ovarian metastases with signet ring cells in a patient with gastric disease should be treated as a Krukenberg tumour until proven otherwise.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Spencer Wells screw clamp for ovariotomy
items.caption: Remember: Spencer Wells clamp = extraperitoneal pedicle clamp for ovariotomy (the stump is held outside the wound).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Ossification of vertebrae
items.caption: Remember: typical vertebra has 3 primary centers (1 centrum + 2 neural arch halves) and 5 secondary centers (spine tip, 2 transverse processes, 2 annular epiphyses), which fuse by about 25 years.
items.author: Cunningham, D. J. (Daniel John), 1850-1909; Robinson, Arthur, b. 1862, ed

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Mogen clamp
items.caption: Remember: Mogen clamp = flat, hinged, slit-bladed steel clamp with a lever lock, used for quick neonatal circumcision.
items.author: Dan Bollinger

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Giardiasis
items.caption: Remember: Giardia = pear-shaped, binucleate 'falling leaf' trophozoites on the duodenal brush border, noninvasive, causing fatty malabsorptive diarrhea; treat with metronidazole or tinidazole.
items.author: Wang, Yuanfei; Gonzalez-Moreno, Olga; Roellig, Dawn M.; Oliver, Laura; Huguet, Jordi; Guo, Yaqiong;

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Gravid uterus at term
items.caption: Remember: the uterus becomes an abdominal organ after 12 weeks, reaches the umbilicus at about 20-22 weeks and the xiphisternum at about 36 weeks.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's mucosa (specialized columnar epithelium)
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = intestinal metaplasia with goblet cells (Alcian blue pH 2.5 positive) replacing squamous epithelium; precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Low-grade endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium
items.caption: Remember: endometrioid adenocarcinoma = back-to-back, crowded glands with little stroma; grade by solid (non-glandular) component: G1 under 5 percent, G2 6-50 percent, G3 over 50 percent; linked to unopposed estrogen and PTEN loss.
items.author: Stewart, Colin J.R.; Crum, Christopher P.; McCluggage, W. Glenn; Park, Kay J.; Rutgers, Joanne K.; O

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gall bladder
items.caption: Remember: the gall bladder lies in a fossa on the visceral surface of the liver along Cantlie's line (IVC to gall bladder fossa).
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Aspiration of gastric/food contents into a bronchiole
items.caption: Remember: Plant cells (thick cellulose walls, clear centers) in airways with clear alveoli and no inflammation = agonal or CPR-related aspiration, not the cause of death.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheal mucosal ulceration from the tube tip with a raised mucosal flap acting as a ball-valve obstruction
items.caption: Remember: a tracheostomy tube tip pressing on the anterior tracheal wall can ulcerate the mucosa and create a flap that acts as a ball valve, causing sudden fatal obstruction on coughing.
items.author: Mark, Leonard Portal

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: the pterion is formed by the frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of the sphenoid (H-shaped); a fracture here tears the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery, causing extradural hematoma.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Hip joint
items.caption: Remember: the iliofemoral (Y) ligament of Bigelow is the strongest ligament in the body.
items.author: Anonymous Unknown author

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Superficial spreading melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Superficial spreading melanoma is the most common subtype (about 70%).
items.author: Juliana Casagrande Tavoloni Braga, Mariana Petaccia Macedo, Clovis Pinto, João Duprat, Maria Dirlei

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's mucosa (intestinal metaplasia of the distal esophagus)
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = columnar metaplasia with goblet cells (Alcian blue pH 2.5 positive acid mucin) replacing squamous epithelium; premalignant for esophageal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic melanoma in lymph node
items.caption: Remember: Metastatic melanoma in a lymph node may be black (melanotic) or tan-white (amelanotic), often both in the same specimen; confirm with S-100, SOX10, HMB-45 and Melan-A.
items.author: Ed Uthman, MD

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Bovine knee (stifle) joint
items.caption: Remember: the stifle is the knee of quadrupeds.
items.author: Museum of Veterinary Anatomy FMVZ USP / Wagner Souza e Silva

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Complete disruption of the right main bronchus (bronchial rupture)
items.caption: Remember: persistent air leak and non-expanding lung despite chest tube after blunt chest trauma = tracheobronchial rupture (usually within 2 cm of the carina, right main bronchus commonly); confirm by bronchoscopy.
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Adenomyosis
items.caption: Remember: Adenomyosis = endometrial glands AND stroma deep in the myometrium (more than 2.5 mm below the basalis); presents with a globular, diffusely enlarged, tender uterus, menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea in multiparous women aged 35-50.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Leprosy
items.caption: Remember: Leprosy granulomas follow nerves and adnexa (perineural, around sweat glands and arrector pili).
items.author: Shiva Raj K.C. Geetika K.C. Purnima Gyawali, Manisha Singh and Milesh Jung Sijapati

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: The sphenoid is the 'keystone' butterfly-shaped bone of the skull base; it articulates with all other cranial bones and contains the optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum, and the sella turcica.
items.author: Images are generated by Japan Life Science Databases(LSDB).

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgeon's knot
items.caption: Remember: surgeon's knot = double wrap on the first throw (2-1 configuration), giving friction that prevents slipping under tension.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Osteosarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Osteosarcoma = malignant spindle cells directly producing osteoid.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Human pineal gland
items.caption: Remember: Corpora arenacea (brain sand) in the pineal gland are calcified concretions.
items.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Posterior view of the thorax and shoulder girdle
items.caption: Remember: on a posterior view of the thorax the scapula spans ribs 2 to 7 (superior angle at T2, spine root at T3, inferior angle at T7), and the clavicle is the only bony link of the shoulder girdle to the axial skeleton.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgical staple remover
items.caption: Remember: a skin staple remover has a lower tongue that slips under the staple crossbar, and squeezing bends the staple in the middle so both legs lift out of the skin; it does not cut.
items.author: Raimond Spekking

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Vermiform appendix
items.caption: Remember: the base of the appendix is found by following the three taeniae coli to their convergence on the caecum; the commonest position is retrocaecal and McBurney's point lies at the junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the spino-umbilical line.
items.author: Hic et nunc

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis)
items.caption: Remember: the normal anterior pituitary is polymorphous, with every hormone present in different cells, whereas an adenoma is monomorphous.
items.author: Jhsteel

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Rathke's pouch (primordium of the adenohypophysis)
items.caption: Remember: anterior pituitary = Rathke's pouch (oral ectoderm, upgrowth); posterior pituitary = infundibulum (neuroectoderm of diencephalon, downgrowth).
items.author: Majumdar S, Farris CL, Kabat BE, Jung DO, Ellsworth BS

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Colorectal adenocarcinoma with lymphatic invasion
items.caption: Remember: tumor emboli in a thin-walled endothelial-lined space within desmoplastic stroma = lymphovascular invasion in colorectal adenocarcinoma, a high-risk feature in stage II disease that favors adjuvant chemotherapy.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Scalpel blade no. 15
items.caption: Remember: No. 15 = small curved blade for fine, short incisions; No.
items.author: JiramJarid

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Melanoma
items.caption: Remember: Sun-damaged elderly head/neck skin with solar elastosis plus crowded atypical melanocytes, pagetoid spread and follicular extension suggests lentigo maligna melanoma; confirm with SOX10/Melan-A.
items.author: Robert M. Hurwitz, Larry J. Buckel, Don-John Summerlin

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Lower end of right humerus, posterior aspect
items.caption: Remember: the olecranon fossa is on the posterior surface of the lower humerus; the coronoid and radial fossae are anterior.
items.author: Wasiul Bahar

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Davis obstetrical forceps
items.caption: Remember: Kielland = sliding lock and minimal pelvic curve (rotation); Wrigley = short outlet forceps; Simpson = English lock and parallel shanks; Piper = aftercoming head of breech with a downward-curved shank.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Gastric amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Congo red with apple-green birefringence under crossed polarizers is diagnostic of amyloid.
items.author: Ed Uthman from Houston, TX, USA

items.subject: mrcp-endocrinology
items.title: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
items.caption: Nuclear grooves, optically clear nuclei and intranuclear pseudoinclusions are the key cytological features of papillary thyroid carcinoma.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Castroviejo-type microsurgical needle holder
items.caption: Remember: a spring-loop handle with a fine tip and a locking catch indicates a Castroviejo-type microsurgical needle holder for 9-0 or finer sutures.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Gallstones (multiple pigment/mixed cholelithiasis)
items.caption: Remember: Multiple faceted stones in a gallbladder = cholelithiasis; most gallstones are cholesterol or mixed, dark pigment stones occur in hemolysis and cirrhosis; treat symptomatic stones with laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
items.author: Xawaari

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Native arteriovenous fistula for hemodialysis access (radiocephalic type)
items.caption: Remember: The Brescia-Cimino fistula (radial artery to cephalic vein at the wrist, non-dominant arm) is the first-choice permanent hemodialysis access; fistula first, graft second, catheter last.
items.author: Pravdaz

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Membranous nephropathy = spike and dome on silver stain, subepithelial deposits on EM, granular IgG/C3 on IF, anti-PLA2R positivity, and the most common cause of adult nephrotic syndrome in Caucasians.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's esophagus
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = columnar (intestinal) metaplasia replacing squamous epithelium of the distal esophagus due to chronic GERD; it is the precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: mrcp-cardiology
items.title: Rheumatic heart disease
items.caption: Rheumatic heart disease diagnosis uses the revised Jones criteria; secondary prophylaxis with benzathine benzylpenicillin or phenoxymethylpenicillin is required after an episode.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis
items.caption: Remember: NEC = premature neonate + enteral feeds + bloody stools + pneumatosis intestinalis (and portal venous gas) on imaging; terminal ileum and proximal colon are the commonest sites.
items.author: CDC / Public Health Image Library

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Laparoscopic appendectomy (three-port technique)
items.caption: Remember: umbilical camera port + two small lower quadrant ports = laparoscopic appendectomy; open appendectomy leaves a single McBurney/Lanz scar in the right iliac fossa.
items.author: KAOSkonfused

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheobronchial injury with complete disruption of the right bronchus intermedius (intermediary trunk)
items.caption: Remember: Blunt tracheobronchial injury usually lies within 2.5 cm of the carina (right more than left).
items.author: Morgan Le Guen, Catherine Beigelman, Belaid Bouhemad, Yang Wenjïe, Frederic Marmion. Modified by use

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Sphenoid bone
items.caption: Remember: Sphenoid = butterfly/bat-shaped central skull base bone with the pterygoid plates, foramen ovale, foramen spinosum, and sella turcica.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Male anatomical wax model (ecorche figure) showing the muscles of the body
items.caption: Remember: Florentine anatomical wax models (Clemente Susini, La Specola, late 18th century) were made to teach anatomy when cadavers were scarce and decayed quickly.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)
items.caption: Remember: DCIS = atypical epithelial proliferation confined within the basement membrane.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. KGH assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Acetabular margin
items.caption: Remember: the acetabular margin is the rim of the socket, deficient inferiorly at the acetabular notch (bridged by the transverse acetabular ligament), and the labrum attaches to it.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: Elderly man + restrictive cardiomyopathy + low-voltage ECG + thick walls + no M protein = wild-type ATTR (senile) amyloidosis; Congo red gives apple-green birefringence, and lipofuscin is a common accompanying finding.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Atlas (C1)
items.caption: Remember: Atlas (C1) has no body and no spinous process; it is a ring of anterior and posterior arches with two lateral masses, and it is the site of Jefferson burst fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Direct inguinal hernia
items.caption: Remember: Direct hernia is medial to the inferior epigastric vessels, through Hesselbach triangle (rectus sheath, inferior epigastric vessels, inguinal ligament).
items.author: Anpol42

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Tracheostomy tube speaking valve (one-way valve)
items.caption: Remember: a speaking valve is a one-way valve at the tracheostomy hub; the cuff MUST be fully deflated before attaching it, or the patient cannot exhale and will suffocate.
items.author: Tenbergen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Membranous nephropathy
items.caption: Remember: Membranous nephropathy = adult nephrotic syndrome, subepithelial deposits, GBM spikes on silver stain, anti-PLA2R antibodies, and risk of renal vein thrombosis.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Axis (C2)
items.caption: Remember: The axis (C2) is the only vertebra with a dens (odontoid process); it is the pivot for rotation of the atlas, and its pars fractures cause a hangman's fracture.
items.author: Anatomography

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Surgeon's knot
items.caption: Remember: Surgeon's knot = double first throw (two wraps around the needle holder) + single opposite second throw.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Circle of Willis
items.caption: Remember: The circle of Willis lies in the interpeduncular cistern, is formed by the ACoA, both ACAs, ICAs, PCoAs and PCAs (with the basilar artery's bifurcation), and is the commonest site of berry aneurysms (ACoA most frequent).
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Microsurgical needle holder (Castroviejo type)
items.caption: Remember: A slender, pencil-grip, spring-action instrument with a gold (tungsten carbide) mark and a small locking catch is a microsurgical (Castroviejo) needle holder, used for 8-0 to 11-0 sutures in replantation and vascular anastomosis.
items.author: Werneuchen

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Alcoholic liver cirrhosis
items.caption: Remember: Alcoholic (Laennec) cirrhosis is classically micronodular (nodules <3 mm); the liver is large and fatty early, then small, shrunken, and fibrotic late.
items.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / Dr. Edwin P. Ewing, Jr.

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Crescentic glomerulonephritis
items.caption: Remember: crescent = parietal epithelial cell and macrophage proliferation in Bowman's space (fibrin-driven); crescents in more than 50 percent of glomeruli = RPGN.
items.author: Arunachalam Ramaswami, Thiraviam Kandaswamy, Tholappan Rajendran, Kizhake Pisharam Jeyakrishnan, Hla

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Senile cardiac amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: elderly patient with restrictive cardiomyopathy, thick ventricle with low-voltage ECG, and pink amorphous extracellular material around myocytes = cardiac amyloidosis (senile ATTRwt); confirm with Congo red apple-green birefringence.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Cryptosporidiosis
items.caption: Remember: Cryptosporidium = tiny basophilic dots on the apical brush border (intracellular, extracytoplasmic); oocysts are acid-fast in stool; AIDS with CD4 less than 100 causes chronic watery diarrhea; treat with nitazoxanide and ART.
items.author: CDC/ Dr. Edwin P. Ewing, Jr.

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Obstetrical forceps
items.caption: Remember: obstetric forceps have two crossing fenestrated blades with cephalic and pelvic curves, a shank, a lock and handles.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Scalpels (bistouries) with fixed and replaceable blades
items.caption: Remember: Bard-Parker handle No.
items.author: No machine-readable author provided. Spekta assumed (based on copyright claims).

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Metastatic Ewing sarcoma
items.caption: Remember: Ewing sarcoma is a small round blue cell tumor with PAS-positive, diastase-sensitive glycogen, CD99 positivity, t(11;22) EWSR1-FLI1, and the lung is the commonest metastatic site.
items.author: Nephron

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Thoracic cage (thorax) viewed from the front
items.caption: Remember: Ribs 1-7 are true (vertebrosternal), 8-10 false (vertebrochondral, forming the costal margin), 11-12 floating (vertebral); the sternal angle (T4/T5 level) marks the 2nd costal cartilage.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Median sagittal section of female pelvis
items.caption: Remember: in a female median sagittal pelvic section the order from front to back is pubis, bladder, uterus/vagina, rectum, sacrum.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Occult wild-type transthyretin (ATTR) cardiac amyloidosis coexisting with aortic stenosis
items.caption: Remember: Grade 2-3 myocardial DPD/PYP/HMDP uptake with no monoclonal protein is diagnostic of ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.
items.author: Thomas A Treibel, Marianna Fontana, Janet A Gilbertson, Karen A Boniface, Steven K White, Amna Abdel

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Triquetral bone
items.caption: Remember: the triquetrum is the pyramidal bone of the proximal row that carries the pisiform on its palmar surface; it is the 2nd most commonly fractured carpal bone (dorsal chip fracture, best seen on lateral view).
items.author: Brian C. Goss

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Nodular melanoma
items.caption: Nodular melanoma: no radial growth phase, early vertical growth, thick at diagnosis.
items.author: Image courtesy of Dr. Ahmet Cemil Kaur Article authors: Zekayi Kutlubay, Burhan Engin, Server Serdar

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Acetabulum
items.caption: Remember: the acetabulum is formed by the ilium (about 2/5), ischium (about 2/5) and pubis (about 1/5), meeting at the Y-shaped triradiate cartilage; its inferior gap (acetabular notch) is bridged by the transverse acetabular ligament.
items.author: BodyParts3D is made by DBCLS

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Pearce obstetrical forceps
items.caption: Remember: Kielland = minimal pelvic curve + sliding lock (rotation); Piper = for the after-coming head in breech; Wrigley = short, outlet/caesarean; Pearce and Simpson-type = fenestrated, pelvic curve, fixed lock for OA delivery.
items.author: Wellcome Collection

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Right inguinal region viewed from within, showing the vessels and structures entering and leaving the abdomen
items.caption: Remember: viewed from within, the inferior epigastric vessels mark the medial margin of the deep inguinal ring.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Anterior compartment muscles of the right leg (anterior view)
items.caption: Remember: the anterior compartment of the leg (tibialis anterior, EHL, EDL, fibularis tertius) is supplied by the deep fibular nerve, dorsiflexes the foot, and its tendons run under the extensor retinacula.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: surgery
items.caption: Remember: A long linear leg wound covered by a meshed split-thickness graft (diamond or net pattern) after compartment syndrome is a skin-grafted fasciotomy; wound left open, closed by delayed primary closure or STSG.
items.author: Bezbozhnik

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Acute transmural appendicitis
items.caption: Remember: the histological criterion for acute appendicitis is neutrophils in the muscularis propria; transmural inflammation with serositis signals impending gangrene or perforation.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
items.caption: Remember: keratin pearls plus intercellular bridges equal squamous cell carcinoma.
items.author: Mikael Häggström

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Lichen amyloidosis
items.caption: Remember: lichen amyloidosis = itchy rippled hyperpigmented papules on the shins; keratin-derived amyloid in the papillary dermis; Congo red positive with apple-green birefringence; caused by chronic friction.
items.author: Georgi Tchernev, Anastasiya Atanasova Chokoeva, Uwe Wollina

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Barrett's mucosa (intestinal metaplasia of the distal esophagus)
items.caption: Remember: Barrett's esophagus = columnar metaplasia with goblet cells (blue on Alcian blue pH 2.5) replacing squamous epithelium of the distal esophagus.
items.author: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP)

items.subject: pathology
items.title: Pheochromocytoma
items.caption: Remember: Pheochromocytoma = Zellballen nests of chromaffin cells with granular amphophilic cytoplasm + S-100 positive sustentacular cells; chromogranin/synaptophysin positive; start alpha-blocker before beta-blocker.
items.author: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of interest: None Mikael Häggström

items.subject: surgery
items.title: Anastomotic leakage after sigmoid resection
items.caption: Remember: a postoperative day 5-8 patient with fever, tachycardia, and rising CRP after colorectal anastomosis has a leak until proven otherwise.
items.author: Hellerhoff

items.subject: anatomy
items.title: Costotransverse joints
items.caption: Remember: costotransverse joints are plane synovial joints between the rib tubercle and the transverse process (T1-T10); the facet is concave in the upper thoracic region and flat in the lower region, and the 11th and 12th ribs have none.
items.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Gynaecological imaging
items.caption: Theca lutein cysts are functional cysts resulting from high beta-HCG levels, seen in molar pregnancy, multifetal gestation, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Neuroradiology
items.caption: The presence of an eccentric scolex within a ring-enhancing brain lesion is pathognomonic for neurocysticercosis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Gastrointestinal
items.caption: Decubitus views are useful in demonstrating air-fluid levels when the patient cannot stand for an erect abdominal film.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Trauma
items.caption: Subdural hematomas are typically venous in origin and characteristically assume a crescent shape on CT, unlike epidural hematomas which are biconvex.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Hepatobiliary
items.caption: The spider web appearance on hepatic venography is pathognomonic for Budd-Chiari syndrome.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Musculoskeletal
items.caption: Greenstick fractures represent incomplete fractures in children where the bone bends and breaks only on the tension side.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Gastrointestinal
items.caption: A mechanical large bowel obstruction can present with secondary small bowel dilation if the ileocaecal valve is incompetent.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Musculoskeletal
items.caption: Paget's disease commonly causes cortical thickening, bowing deformities, and characteristic incomplete cortical fractures.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Neuroradiology
items.caption: Pilocytic astrocytomas, often associated with NF1, typically present as cystic lesions with a non-enhancing wall and an enhancing mural nodule.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Rolling hiatus hernia
items.caption: In a rolling hiatus hernia, the gastro-oesophageal junction remains in its normal anatomical position.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Osteosarcoma
items.caption: Look for the sun-ray appearance and Codman triangle as specific signs of osteosarcoma on imaging.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Posterior malleolus
items.caption: The posterior malleolus is a key component of the distal tibia that must be evaluated on lateral ankle radiographs.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Batwing distribution
items.caption: Batwing distribution is also known as butterfly shadow, reflecting the distribution of pulmonary oedema.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Intussusception
items.caption: Always look for the empty right iliac fossa sign to support a diagnosis of intussusception.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Asbestosis
items.caption: Calcified pleural plaques are a key diagnostic clue for asbestos-related disease.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Osteoarthritis
items.caption: Medial joint space narrowing combined with osteophytes is the classic radiological presentation of knee osteoarthritis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Cervical spondylosis
items.caption: Lipping of the vertebral bodies is a classic degenerative marker seen in cervical spondylosis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Osteoarthritis
items.caption: Look for osteophytes and subarticular sclerosis to distinguish degenerative osteoarthritis from inflammatory arthritides like rheumatoid arthritis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
items.caption: Always look for the absence of osteophytes and the presence of erosions to distinguish inflammatory rheumatoid arthritis from degenerative osteoarthritis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Osteochondroma
items.caption: Osteochondroma is the most common benign bone tumour.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Monteggia fracture-dislocation
items.caption: The radial head should always point to the capitellum on all views; if it does not, suspect a Monteggia injury.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Transependymal CSF spread
items.caption: Sulcal effacement and transependymal CSF spread are key indicators of raised intracranial pressure in hydrocephalus.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Lateral and medial malleolus
items.caption: Ensure the ankle mortice is even throughout when evaluating radiographs for potential fractures.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Lateral masses of the Atlas
items.caption: Always check for symmetry of the lateral masses of the atlas relative to the axis on the open mouth view.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Bilateral diffuse airspace consolidation
items.caption: ARDS is a non-cardiogenic condition; look for the absence of cardiomegaly on the chest X-ray.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Periosteal reaction
items.caption: A sequestrum is a hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis appearing as a dense bone fragment within a lytic lesion.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: A normal cervical spine
items.caption: The posterior vertebral line is the most important alignment marker as it is least affected by osteophytes.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Crescent-shaped hyperdensity
items.caption: SDH is crescent-shaped and not limited by sutures.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Lumbar spondylosis
items.caption: Reduced disc spaces combined with osteophytes are the radiological hallmarks of lumbar spondylosis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Giant bullous emphysema
items.caption: Bullae are distinguished from pneumothorax by the presence of thin curvilinear walls and lack of a pleural line.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
items.caption: Always look for bowel loops in the hemithorax when a neonate has respiratory distress and mediastinal shift.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Water-lily sign
items.caption: The water-lily sign is pathognomonic for a ruptured hydatid cyst where the endocyst membrane collapses into the fluid.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Skier's thumb
items.caption: Skier's thumb is specifically associated with ulnar collateral ligament disruption.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Tram tracking
items.caption: Tram tracking is a highly specific sign for bronchial wall thickening in bronchiectasis.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Cervical vertebra
items.caption: The presence of transverse foramina is the most reliable anatomical marker to distinguish a cervical vertebra from other spinal segments.

items.subject: radiology
items.title: Perched facets
items.caption: A step deformity of greater than 3mm on a lateral cervical spine X-ray indicates an unstable spine.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Myoid hamartoma
items.caption: Consider myoid hamartoma in the differential of a breast mass containing adipose tissue and smooth muscle bundles that stain positive for SMA and desmin.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Bird's beak sign
items.caption: Always consider pseudoachalasia in patients with a bird's beak appearance if there is rapid symptom progression or atypical features on endoscopy.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Perform a bone marrow biopsy and aspirate at a site of focal lesion identified on WB DW-MRI
items.caption: Whole-body MRI with diffusion-weighted sequences is the preferred imaging modality for the initial workup and staging of myeloma, offering superior sensitivity for occult focal lesions.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Bone tumours
items.caption: Osteofibrous dysplasia is a 'touch-me-not' lesion often managed conservatively, typically occurring in the tibial diaphysis of young children.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Lemierre syndrome
items.caption: Think of Lemierre syndrome in any patient with a recent pharyngitis who develops persistent fever and neck swelling, even if the initial presentation was misdiagnosed as viral.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
items.caption: In a premenopausal woman, the combination of diffuse round pulmonary cysts and a renal or retroperitoneal angiomyolipoma is pathognomonic for lymphangioleiomyomatosis.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Vascular
items.caption: Atherosclerosis is a common process in patients over 45 years, manifesting as calcified, irregular plaque formation in large and medium-sized arteries.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Mirror image artefact
items.caption: Mirror image artefact in the trachea arises from the highly reflective air-mucosa interface, often leading to the false appearance of deeper structures within the tracheal lumen.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Paediatric Hip
items.caption: The Kocher criteria (fever, non-weight bearing, elevated inflammatory markers, leukocytosis) are essential for distinguishing septic arthritis from transient synovitis in children with hip effusions.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Cerebrospinal fluid HSV-1 polymerase chain reaction
items.caption: In patients with acute confusion and temporal lobe abnormalities on MRI, suspect HSVE and initiate empiric acyclovir before waiting for PCR confirmation.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Malrotation with midgut volvulus
items.caption: The whirlpool sign on cross-sectional imaging is a high-specificity indicator of mesenteric torsion and midgut volvulus.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Musculoskeletal
items.caption: Lateral cortical thickening in the femoral shaft is highly suggestive of bisphosphonate-related fracture.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Increased thickness of the pericardium on CT
items.caption: Look for pericardial calcification or thickening >4 mm on CT to confirm constrictive pericarditis when clinical signs of right heart failure are present.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Fetal anomalies
items.caption: Nuchal translucency > 3 mm in the first trimester is a marker for chromosomal abnormalities and requires further evaluation.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Temporal bone
items.caption: Scutum erosion and opacification of Prussak's space are the earliest and most common radiological signs of a pars flaccida cholesteatoma.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Coil embolization of the splenic artery proximal and distal to the pseudoaneurysm
items.caption: Exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm sac by proximal and distal coil embolization is the gold standard, ensuring no retrograde filling occurs.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Paranasal sinuses
items.caption: A concha bullosa is a common anatomical variant that is typically asymptomatic but can rarely cause nasal obstruction.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Congenital brain malformations
items.caption: Colpocephaly refers to the disproportionate enlargement of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles due to callosal dysgenesis.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Nasolacrimal apparatus
items.caption: A dacryocystocele results from nasolacrimal duct obstruction and may present to the emergency department when secondarily infected as dacryocystitis.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Omental cake
items.caption: Omental cake is pathognomonic for extensive peritoneal metastatic disease and is most frequently associated with ovarian, gastric, or colon cancer.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Foot
items.caption: Plantar fasciitis is usually a clinical diagnosis, but MRI shows thickening and increased T2 signal at the calcaneal insertion.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Pulmonary artery filling defects
items.caption: In patients with acute abdominal pain and unremarkable abdominal imaging, always consider pulmonary embolism, especially if the D-dimer is elevated or there is unexplained tachycardia.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Stomach
items.caption: Gastric GISTs frequently present as large, lobulated, submucosal masses with variable intramural, endogastric, or exogastric extension.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Obstetrics
items.caption: The yolk sac is the earliest structure identified within the gestational sac and should typically be visible when the sac diameter reaches 8 mm.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Bear's paw sign
items.caption: The bear's paw sign, characterized by multiloculated low-attenuation areas replacing the renal parenchyma, should always raise suspicion for XGP in the context of a staghorn calculus.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Shock-related thyroid change
items.caption: In a polytrauma patient, symmetric perithyroidal fluid with preserved thyroid morphology is a marker of hypoperfusion rather than direct neck trauma.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Measurement of serum factor XIII activity
items.caption: In spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage with normal routine coagulation panels, always consider factor XIII deficiency.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Congenital heart disease
items.caption: Cor triatriatum sinistrum acts functionally like mitral stenosis and can cause unexplained pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary oedema.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Neuroblastoma
items.caption: In a child with a suprarenal mass, elevated urinary VMA levels should prompt a diagnosis of neuroblastoma regardless of cystic or hemorrhagic imaging appearances.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle
items.caption: A midline cystic lesion at the foramen of Monro causing obstructive hydrocephalus should be considered a colloid cyst regardless of atypical signal characteristics.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Ureterocele with duplex kidney
items.caption: The presence of a bladder-base filling defect in a female infant should raise immediate suspicion for a duplex system with an ectopic ureterocele.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Paediatric
items.caption: Always consider VACTERL association when esophageal atresia is identified on a chest radiograph.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
items.caption: Langerhans cell histiocytosis should be considered in children presenting with unexplained lytic bone lesions and soft tissue swellings.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Fluid-fluid levels
items.caption: The presence of fluid-fluid levels on MRI in a bone lesion is highly suggestive of an aneurysmal bone cyst, but one must always exclude telangiectatic osteosarcoma.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
items.caption: In elderly patients with unexplained right heart failure and right-sided volume overload, always consider PAPVR with an associated sinus venosus ASD despite negative initial echocardiography.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
items.caption: Porcelain gallbladder is no longer considered an absolute indication for radical resection, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the preferred management.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Infantile hepatic haemangioma
items.caption: In infants with five or more cutaneous hemangiomas, screening abdominal ultrasound is mandatory to exclude visceral involvement, specifically IHH.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Paediatric Radiology
items.caption: Incomplete resection of the coccyx during surgery for sacrococcygeal teratoma is associated with a high recurrence rate.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Skull base pathology
items.caption: Paget disease of the skull presents with lytic (osteolysis circumscripta) and sclerotic phases, with deafness being the most common clinical complication.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome
items.caption: Think of PRES when encountering symmetric, subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the posterior hemispheres during a hypertensive emergency.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Late gadolinium enhancement inversion recovery sequence
items.caption: Subendocardial enhancement in a coronary territory is the hallmark of ischemic myocardial infarction on LGE-CMR.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Oesophagus
items.caption: Distension of the esophagus is crucial during barium studies to differentiate varices from varicoid carcinoma.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Perilymphatic distribution
items.caption: In sarcoidosis, look for perilymphatic nodules tracking along the fissures, bronchovascular bundles, and pleural surfaces.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Vascular
items.caption: Duplicated inferior vena cava is frequently associated with renal anomalies like horseshoe or crossed fused ectopic kidneys.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
items.caption: In a patient with acute flank pain and normal urinalysis, a disproportionately elevated LDH level should raise suspicion for renal infarction.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Pneumatosis intestinalis
items.caption: Pneumatosis intestinalis is the pathognomonic radiological sign of necrotizing enterocolitis, appearing as linear lucencies in the bowel wall.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Pelvic vasculature
items.caption: The corona mortis is a high-risk vascular anastomosis that can cause life-threatening haemorrhage during pelvic surgery or trauma.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Ankle
items.caption: The Master Knot of Henry represents the site where the flexor digitorum longus tendon crosses over the flexor hallucis longus tendon.

items.subject: ss-radiology
items.title: Aorta
